title: Wereld dichter bij gendergelijkheid dan ooit
content:
De wereld is vandaag dichter bij gelijkheid tussen man en vrouw dan ooit. Dat blijkt uit het Global Gender Gap Report 2026. De vooruitgang van de voorbije twintig jaar is duidelijk, al blijft ze op sommige plaatsen kwetsbaar.
Twintig jaar geleden bracht het World Economic Forum voor het eerst de wereldwijde genderkloof in kaart. De nieuwste editie van het Global Gender Gap Report toont dat er sindsdien duidelijke vooruitgang is geboekt.
Wereldwijd is de genderkloof vandaag voor 69,2 procent gedicht. Dat is 0,4 procentpunt meer dan vorig jaar. Ook bekleden veel meer vrouwen leidinggevende functies in het bedrijfsleven en bij de overheid dan in 2006.
“De gegevens van de afgelopen twintig jaar tonen dat gendergelijkheid haalbaar is”, zegt Saadia Zahidi, directeur bij het World Economic Forum. “Economieën op elk inkomensniveau hebben vooruitgang geboekt, dus het gebrek aan middelen is geen belemmering.”
IJsland blijft koploper
Voor het rapport werden 145 economieën vergeleken op vier domeinen: economische participatie en kansen, gezondheid en levensverwachting, opleidingsniveau en politieke zeggenschap.
IJsland staat voor de zeventiende keer bovenaan de ranglijst en heeft 93 procent van de genderkloof gedicht. Finland volgt met 87,2 procent, Noorwegen met 85,7 procent.
Ook Namibië maakt een opvallende sprong. Het land klom vier plaatsen naar de vierde plaats en is met 84,5 procent het hoogst genoteerde land in Afrika ten zuiden van de Sahara.
Verder staan het Verenigd Koninkrijk, Nieuw-Zeeland, Zweden, Australië, Duitsland en Ierland in de top tien.
Meer vrouwen in politiek
Vooral op politiek vlak is er over een periode van twintig jaar vooruitgang geboekt. De score voor politieke zeggenschap steeg met 8 procentpunt in de landen die in het onderzoek werden meegenomen.
In 2006 was er één vrouwelijke minister per 8,1 mannen. Vandaag is dat één vrouw per 4,3 mannen. Ook in parlementen is de verhouding verbeterd: van één vrouw per 5,6 mannen naar ongeveer één per drie.
Toch blijft politieke vertegenwoordiging een van de domeinen waar de grootste kloof bestaat. De wereldwijde score voor politieke zeggenschap bedraagt 22,1 procent. Voor economische participatie en kansen is dat 61,7 procent.
Vooruitgang is niet vanzelfsprekend
De cijfers tonen tegelijk dat vooruitgang niet automatisch blijft doorgaan. De wereldwijde score voor politieke zeggenschap ligt vandaag lager dan in 2016 en daalde het voorbije jaar nog met 0,4 procentpunt.
Aan het huidige tempo zou het nog 120 jaar duren voor volledige gelijkheid op de vier onderzochte domeinen bereikt is.
Ook België toont dat vooruitgang niet altijd in één rechte lijn verloopt. Ons land stond in 2023 nog op de tiende plaats, maar is intussen gezakt naar plaats 33. Nederland staat op plaats 46 en haalde sinds 2008 de top tien niet meer.
Volgens Zahidi is het daarom belangrijk om voort te bouwen op wat werkt. “Om dit proces te versnellen, moeten overheden en werkgevers lessen trekken uit beleid dat werkt en dit sneller toepassen.”
De balans na twintig jaar is daarmee dubbel maar hoopgevend: de genderkloof is kleiner geworden en landen op elk inkomensniveau hebben vooruitgang geboekt. Tegelijk toont het rapport dat verdere vooruitgang inspanning blijft vragen.

title: Liberia: Liberia's Electricity Access Hits 39 Percent
content:
MONROVIA — Liberia's electricity access rate has increased from 32 percent to 39 percent, according to the government, as the Liberia Electricity Corporation (LEC) moves to expand power connections to more counties and underserved communities.
Deputy Information Minister for Press and Public Affairs Daniel Sanoe disclosed the figures Tuesday, September 22, during the Ministry of Information's regular press briefing in Monrovia.
Sanoe said the increase was highlighted during a government review of progress under the National Development Plan, as authorities continue efforts to extend electricity beyond communities already connected to the national grid.
Despite the reported increase, a significant portion of Liberia's population remains without access to electricity, particularly in rural communities outside major population centers.

Sanoe disclosed that LEC recently concluded a two-day technical assessment in Lofa and Grand Cape Mount counties to determine the feasibility of extending electricity to additional communities.
The assessment covered communities along key corridors, including areas around the Lofa Bridge and a mining hub in Grand Cape Mount County.
According to Sanoe, the assessment team inspected public and private facilities identified as potential beneficiaries of grid expansion, including hospitals, government facilities, businesses and other essential institutions.
LEC officials also met with community leaders, traditional authorities and youth representatives to discuss the proposed expansion and possible arrangements for connecting communities to the national grid.
The technical assessment is expected to help determine the feasibility of extending electricity lines and developing distribution networks in the targeted areas.
The reported increase from 32 percent to 39 percent represents a seven-percentage-point rise in electricity access. However, it also means that a majority of the population remains without electricity if the government figures are applied nationally.
For communities still outside the grid, reliable electricity remains critical to expanding economic activity and improving access to education, healthcare and other essential services.
Sanoe said LEC will continue efforts to extend electricity to additional counties and communities as part of the government's broader energy expansion program.
The challenge, however, remains translating increases in the national electricity-access rate into reliable and sustainable power for communities that have remained outside Liberia's electricity network.

title: Kansas rancher says 50 wind turbines now supply half his income, help keep ranch in family
content:
A Kansas rancher who once worried that wind turbines might change his land says they ultimately did something even more meaningful: They helped keep his ranch in the family.
Since 2006, the 50 turbines on Peter Ferrell's ranch have supplied about half of his income, helping steady a business where revenue can swing widely from year to year.
Here's what to know
In the Flint Hills, Ferrell, a fourth-generation rancher, did not immediately agree to host a wind power project that would become the largest in Kansas. As Good News Network reported, he had to weigh the same objections many rural landowners still hear: that turbines would scar the landscape, endanger prairie chickens, or bring in money seen as out of step with ranching culture.
Ferrell said the turbines have turned out to be easy neighbors, and the biggest change has been economic rather than ecological. The added income has helped protect the ranch from the boom-and-bust nature of cattle production, while cattle still graze the land, the prairie remains intact, and prairie chickens continue to nest there.
After Greenlight Energy Resources took on the development, the effort became the Elk River Wind Power project, which now powers 60,000 homes. That kind of energy generation can help communities reduce their reliance on dirtier power sources while expanding access to electricity produced without fuel costs that can fluctuate over time.
Ferrell said the decision was rooted as much in stewardship as in economics.
"My family has been here since 1888, and that weighs heavily on my decision to engage in practices that can be carried on generation after generation without depleting the resources," he said in a statement. "Both the grass and the wind will be here for generations."
More background
For landowners, wind projects can provide dependable royalty income without requiring them to give up the primary use of their land.
That is especially important in agriculture, where debt, weather, and commodity prices can make it difficult for farms and ranches to survive across generations. A second income stream can help families cover costs, ease financial pressure, and avoid selling land that has been in the family for decades.
Wind power can strengthen local tax bases, create jobs tied to construction and maintenance, and reduce air pollution from fossil fuel generation — a public health benefit that can be especially meaningful for communities downwind of power plants.
Ferrell said that stability has reshaped what is possible for his family's future.
"I have two grown children and four grandkids, and they love this place," he said. "Because of the wind farm, they'll be able to perpetuate it without financial burden."
What's being done?
Across the country, developers, utilities, and landowners are increasingly embracing "working lands" models that allow clean energy projects to coexist with farming and ranching. Ferrell's ranch is one example: The turbines occupy part of the property, but the cattle operation continues.
This kind of dual use does not require an all-or-nothing decision. Families can continue producing food, preserve open land, and add income that helps pay bills and plan for the next generation.
He has also become someone other ranchers turn to when they are considering the same option.
"After the wind farm was built, my phone rang off the hook," Ferrell said. "Farmers and ranchers asking, 'How'd you do it? Could we get one?'"
Where can I learn more?
Wind power can bolster rural economies without pushing agriculture aside. In places such as Kansas and Iowa, that has meant new income for farms and local communities, while major projects off coastal Virginia show how those benefits can grow on a much larger scale.
• On another Kansas ranch, expenses almost prevented him from keeping the farm at all.
• In Howard County, Iowa, wind development generated nearly $3 million for a small farm community.
• Off the coast of Virginia, Dominion Energy completed a major offshore build with broad economic stakes.

title: Pilotprojekt in Pankow erleichtert Wohnungslosen die Wahlteilnahme
content: Ein Pilotprojekt in Pankow bringt Verwaltung und soziale Einrichtungen zusammen und unterstützt Wohnungslose direkt vor Ort bei der Anmeldung und bei der Stimmabgabe. Eine eigene Wohnung braucht es nicht, um in Berlin mitzubestimmen. Auch Menschen ohne festen Wohnsitz dürfen bei der Wahl zum Abgeordnetenhaus am 20. September ihre Stimme abgeben. Doch das Wählen ist für viele Menschen ohne festen Wohnsitz mit Hürden verbunden. Im Rahmen eines Pilotprojekts im Bezirk Pankow helfen Mitarbeitende des Bezirks, der Diakonie, der Immanuel-Beratung und der Landesarmutskonferenz wohnungslosen Menschen direkt in einer Tagesstätte der Diakonie. Da Menschen ohne festen Wohnsitz nicht automatisch im Wählerverzeichnis stehen, müssen sie sich für die Wahl anmelden. Dabei bekommen sie vor Ort Unterstützung. Verwaltung und Sozialarbeit arbeiten zusammen Wer möchte, kann anschließend sogar direkt per Briefwahl abstimmen. Für die Diakonie ist das Projekt ein wichtiger Beitrag zur gesellschaftlichen Teilhabe. Es zeigt, wie Verwaltung und soziale Einrichtungen gemeinsam Hürden abbauen können. Das Wahlamt sorgt für ein rechtssicheres Verfahren, während die Sozialarbeit den direkten Zugang zu den Menschen ermöglicht. Gerade für Menschen ohne festen Wohnsitz kann dieser persönliche Kontakt entscheidend sein. Denn viele wissen laut Bundesarbeitsgemeinschaft Wohnungslosenhilfe gar nicht, dass sie wählen dürfen oder welche Schritte dafür nötig sind. Eine Stimme, die zählt Grundsätzlich gelten für Menschen ohne festen Wohnsitz dieselben Voraussetzungen wie für andere Wahlberechtigte. Sie müssen Deutsche und mindestens 16 Jahre alt sein und seit mindestens drei Monaten in Berlin leben. Das Projekt macht deutlich: Demokratie soll nicht davon abhängen, ob jemand eine feste Adresse hat. Mit praktischer Unterstützung kann politische Teilhabe für mehr Menschen erreichbar werden. title: Lọc máu cho người suy thận kèm HIV
content:
Lọc máu cho người suy thận kèm HIV
TP HCMÔng Kiên, 50 tuổi, suy thận cấp trên nền bệnh thận mạn và HIV, được lọc máu cấp cứu và điều trị các bệnh nền giúp hồi phục sau ba tháng.
Ông Kiên đến Trung tâm Tiết niệu - Thận học - Nam khoa, Bệnh viện Đa khoa Tâm Anh TP HCM tái khám hồi giữa tháng 9. Xét nghiệm cho thấy độ lọc cầu thận đạt 59 ml/phút/1,73m², về mức bệnh thận mạn giai đoạn 3A, bệnh nhân không còn phải lọc máu. BS.CKI Mạch Thị Chúc Linh, khoa Nội thận - Lọc máu, cho biết ông Kiên trong nhóm bệnh nhân đặc biệt được điều trị tổn thương thận cấp trên nền bệnh thận mạn kèm bệnh nền HIV, tăng huyết áp, đái tháo đường và viêm gan C.
10 năm nay, ông Kiên điều trị ổn định bệnh thận mạn giai đoạn 3A và uống thuốc điều trị theo phác đồ ARV để ức chế virus HIV. Giữa tháng 7/2024, ông đột ngột ngất xỉu, cấp cứu ở bệnh viện địa phương xét nghiệm ghi nhận chức năng thận suy giảm, ure tăng gấp 3 lần bình thường, creatinine tăng vọt gấp gần 10 lần. Ông được đặt catheter (ống thông nhỏ) tĩnh mạch đùi lọc máu cấp cứu, thoát nguy kịch nhưng cần tiếp tục lọc máu và theo dõi lâu dài, được khoa Nội thận - Lọc máu, Bệnh viện Đa khoa Tâm Anh tiếp nhận.
Bác sĩ Linh cho biết người nhiễm HIV khi mắc bệnh thận phải được kiểm soát nhiễm khuẩn chặt chẽ. Quá trình lọc máu không chỉ nhằm thay thế tạm thời chức năng thận mà cần đồng thời kiểm soát nhiễm trùng, rà soát thuốc, duy trì điều trị ARV và theo dõi các bệnh nền.
Theo bác sĩ Linh, bệnh nhân HIV vốn đã suy giảm sức đề kháng, việc lọc máu nhiều lần mỗi tuần đòi hỏi phải chọc kim vào mạch máu hoặc duy trì catheter. Chỉ cần nhiễm trùng tại vị trí đường vào mạch máu cũng có thể tiến triển thành nhiễm khuẩn huyết, nặng hơn là sốc nhiễm trùng. Đặc biệt, catheter lọc máu có nguy cơ nhiễm khuẩn cao hơn nhiều so với cầu nối động-tĩnh mạch (AVF).
Bác sĩ đánh giá ông Kiên vẫn duy trì lượng nước tiểu tốt, không bị ứ dịch và cân nặng gần như ổn định nên vẫn còn khả năng hồi phục chức năng thận. Êkíp vừa lọc máu hỗ trợ vừa theo dõi khả năng hồi phục của thận.
Ông được lọc máu cấp cứu không siêu lọc 2 lần/tuần để loại bỏ các chất độc, không rút dịch, đồng thời theo dõi lượng nước tiểu, cân nặng, huyết áp, điện giải và diễn tiến chức năng thận. Theo bác sĩ Linh, việc không rút nước giúp duy trì thể tích tuần hoàn và tưới máu thận, tạo điều kiện cho phần mô thận còn khả năng hồi phục chức năng.
Người bệnh nhiễm HIV nên biến chứng phức tạp hơn, các chất độc hại tích tụ, đối mặt với phù phổi, suy tim, tăng kali máu và hội chứng ure huyết cao. Bác sĩ điều chỉnh thuốc kháng virus theo độ lọc cầu thận, tránh làm tăng nặng các bệnh nền liên quan. Ông Kiên được bố trí lọc máu tại phòng riêng, sử dụng máy lọc chuyên biệt đi kèm hệ thống dây quả lọc sử dụng một lần và tiêu hủy theo quy trình.
Chức năng thận của ông Kiên dần hồi phục, từ trên 30 ml/phút/1,73m² về gần mức nền, creatinine giảm xuống 6 lần so với thời điểm cấp cứu, còn hơn 200 µmol/L. Sau 3 tháng, ông Kiên được ngừng lọc máu cấp cứu, chuyển sang theo dõi ngoại trú, tái khám định kỳ và uống thuốc theo chỉ định để duy trì chức năng thận ổn định.
Bác sĩ Linh cho biết trước đây người bệnh HIV bị suy thận gặp khó khăn để tìm nơi lọc máu định kỳ, do nhiều cơ sở y tế thiếu trang thiết bị cách ly chuyên biệt. Hiện, nhiều cơ sở y tế chủ động bố trí hệ thống phòng lọc máu và máy lọc riêng biệt cho bệnh nhân HIV, áp dụng quy trình kiểm soát nhiễm khuẩn nghiêm ngặt giúp người bệnh lọc máu an toàn kết hợp điều trị liệu pháp ART.
Bác sĩ lưu ý người bệnh thận mạn có bệnh nền HIV không tự ý sử dụng các loại nước lá hoặc bài thuốc truyền miệng không rõ nguồn gốc vì nguy cơ chứa các thành phần gây tổn thương thận. Nếu có dấu hiệu mệt nhiều, phù, tiểu ít, buồn nôn, khó thở hoặc các bất thường sau khi sử dụng một loại thuốc, nước lá hay sản phẩm không rõ nguồn gốc, người bệnh cần đến bệnh viện khám sớm để can thiệp kịp thời.
Tổn thương thận cấp nếu phát hiện và xử trí kịp thời có cơ hội hồi phục đáng kể. Tổn thương nặng hoặc kéo dài có thể khiến chức năng thận suy giảm thêm và làm tăng nguy cơ tiến triển bệnh.

title: World-first ENT surgery performed aboard aircraft in Bishkek
content:
Chinese surgeons performed surgery on a patient with allergic rhinitis aboard a hospital aircraft at Manas Airport in Bishkek. It was the first time such an ENT procedure had been performed aboard an aircraft anywhere in the world.
According to the Chinese Embassy, a C909 aircraft of Chinese aircraft manufacturer COMAC arrived in Kyrgyzstan as part of the charitable Air Silk Road of Health mission. The plane is equipped with an operating suite for performing ophthalmological and ENT surgeries.
Sun Xicai, Chief Physician of the Otorhinolaryngology Department at Fudan University Hospital, explained that a minimally invasive technique developed by his team was selected for the patient’s treatment. He noted that this method minimizes tissue trauma.
This is the first time globally that such a surgery has been performed on an aircraft.
Sun Xicai
The procedure was performed under local anaesthesia. According to the surgeon, the patient remained calm and experienced no pain or discomfort. Recovery is expected to take from one to two weeks, after which a follow-up examination will be required.
Sun Xicai noted that the advantage of the flying hospital is its readiness for immediate operation upon arrival. The equipment is already installed, the layout of devices and instruments has been carefully planned, and the surgical workflow is fine-tuned. Moving all of this to another clinic, the doctor explains, would require preparing the facilities and organizing operations all over again.

title: Genetic testing program pioneered in Maritimes improving cancer care in Canada
content:
A genetic testing program that helps rule out a stem-cell donor due to a genetic risk for developing leukemia was pioneered in the Maritimes and is helping to improve cancer care in Canada.
Ryan White credits the work at the IWK Maritime Centre for Precision Medicine in Halifax for saving his life.
“I think the odds, if I didn’t have this testing through Precision Medicine, like I don’t think I’d be here today,” he said.
Back in 2020, White was feeling short of breath and had low energy, so he decided to seek medical help.
Soon, he learned he had a rare form of leukemia.
“It’s a disease called acute myeloid leukemia, so it’s a blood cancer. It’s (a) very quick progression if it’s not caught in time,” he said.
He was treated in May 2020 with chemotherapy, and despite going into remission, the cancer came back later that year.
This time, he needed a bone marrow transplant.
“I was home for a few weeks and then found out. It was an unfortunate Christmas present that I came out of remission in December and then had to go back for a second round of testing,” he recalled.
“That first trial didn’t work, (so) we went straight to that level three. And they prepared me for a bone marrow transplant, so more chemotherapy and then ultimately leading up into a bone-marrow transplant.”
Get weekly health news
It was at this point that hereditary genetic testing was used to help create his treatment plan. The testing was done as part of Canada’s first clinical program focused on hereditary myeloid malignancies, which was developed by hematologist Dr. Amy Trottier.
Trottier says in White’s case, testing showed he had a hereditary predisposition for the cancer.
“And that was the reason why it came back — because although his leukemia was cured, he still had that genetic change that would just keep making leukemia happen,” said Trottier.
That key detail can be used to rule out potential bone marrow transplant donors.
“Originally, when he was being worked up for transplant before we actually had this genetic test result back (…) one of his siblings was found to be a perfect match,” said Trottier.
“And they were going to be the planned donor. Fortunately, we got this result back in time.”
Armed with this new information, an alternative donor was identified and White’s treatment plan was designed around his unique genetic factors that contributed to his disease.
“Based on that overall genetic disposition, they were really able to hone down the pathway (for the) types of chemotherapy, how long, how many doses I need,” he said.
“And then what the follow-up plan looked like and then ultimately leading into my bone marrow transplant.”
IWK Health is one of only two centres in Canada offering this specialized testing, and has now become a referral centre for the rest of the country.
“People often think of IWK as a women’s and children’s hospital. What people sometimes don’t realize is that our genetics and genomics teams here actually treat people across the lifespan, so not only women and children,” said Lee Anne Boutilier, Precision Medicine’s director.
For White, the ability to access the testing was life-changing. He says his recovery wasn’t an easy road by any means, but he’s “happy to be on this side of the grass.”
“Once I had the bone marrow transplant, I was home, I started to process things. There was a depression trying to figure out why me, why this had to happen,” he said.
He says he learned to “recognize that life is short” and to “just stop and smell the roses and experience things.”
“Just enjoy the people around me, my wife, my mother, my father, and my sister, and focus in on the positives within my life. So, ironically, getting back to going to the gym, getting out gardening, going mountain biking,” he said.
And he’s thankful for the team at the IWK for helping him have this opportunity, he says.
“It was a tough journey, but my health has been great over the last several years. April the 8th was my fifth-year anniversary of being in remission, essentially and I really credit the Centre for Precision Medicine with saving my life,” he said.

title: “Impareremo anche in una tenda”: a Gaza i bambini tornano a scuola dopo quasi tre anni, tra le macerie e il desiderio di ricominciare
content:
“Impareremo anche in una tenda”: a Gaza i bambini tornano a scuola dopo quasi tre anni, tra le macerie e il desiderio di ricominciare
Indice
Per molte bambine e molti bambini del mondo, il primo giorno di scuola significa indossare un grembiule nuovo, aprire un quaderno ancora intatto e ritrovare i compagni in un’aula pronta ad accoglierli. A Gaza, il ritorno a scuola ha invece decisamente un altro volto.
Per la prima volta dopo quasi tre anni, centinaia di migliaia di studenti sono tornati alla didattica in presenza, ma la stragrande maggioranza non ha trovato edifici scolastici ricostruiti: le lezioni sono ripartite in scuole danneggiate, strutture improvvisate e tende allestite per accogliere gli studenti.
Leggi anche: Crolla un edificio (bombardato) a Gaza: almeno 12 morti, fra cui bambini, si scava a mani nude per cercare i dispersi
Un ritorno fragile, segnato dalle conseguenze dei raid israeliani, ma pensiamoci un secondo: per molti rappresenta anche la possibilità di riappropriarsi di una parte della propria quotidianità.
Il 98% delle scuole danneggiato o distrutto
Secondo UNICEF, il 98% delle scuole nella Striscia di Gaza è stato distrutto o danneggiato durante il conflitto. Gli uffici dell’istruzione di Gaza stimano che circa 660 mila studenti siano rimasti privati della possibilità di frequentare regolarmente le lezioni in presenza.
La riapertura delle scuole arriva quindi in un contesto estremamente complesso: molte famiglie non possono permettersi uniformi, quaderni e penne, beni che prima della guerra erano facilmente accessibili.Il nuovo anno scolastico è iniziato, quindi, con un numero significativo di difficoltà materiali, ma anche con il tentativo di ricostruire urgentemente gli spazi dedicati all’infanzia e all’apprendimento.
“Impareremo anche in una tenda”
A Khan Younis, nel sud della Striscia di Gaza, alcuni studenti hanno raccontato dalle pagine di RTE cosa significhi tornare in classe dopo anni di interruzione.
L’ultima volta che sono andato a scuola è stato tre anni fa. Ora iniziamo l’anno scolastico, è un anno di gioia, felicità e successo, ha raccontato uno studente.
Un altro ragazzo ha spiegato di voler continuare a studiare nonostante le condizioni difficili: frequenterà le lezioni seduto sul pavimento di una tenda senza una ventilazione adeguata, senza scarpe in buone condizioni e senza quaderno o penna.
Durante i bombardamenti ha perso degli amici, ma non vuole rinunciare alla scuola.
Nonostante tutto questo impareremo, impareremo anche in una tenda, ha detto.
Le nuove scuole nascono dove è possibile
Nonostante la distruzione, il Ministero dell’Istruzione di Gaza, con il sostegno di organizzazioni locali e internazionali, ha deciso di far partire l’anno scolastico 2026-2027. Per farlo sono state create decine di scuole temporanee realizzate con tende, teloni, lamiere e legno. Alcune sorgono su terreni sabbiosi. Altre hanno aule con pochi materassi e una lavagna. In alcune strutture gli studenti si affollano negli spazi disponibili, mentre altri edifici scolastici continuano ancora a ospitare famiglie sfollate.
Secondo gli uffici dell’istruzione, almeno 540 mila studenti dovrebbero frequentare quest’anno lezioni in presenza all’interno di scuole private improvvisate, centri temporanei di apprendimento e altri spazi educativi, con il sostegno dell’UNICEF.
Per chi non può frequentare o per chi ha lasciato Gaza durante la guerra continuerà invece la formazione online.
Il ritorno a scuola non cancella le ferite e non restituisce alle bambine e ai bambini ciò che hanno perso. Ma per migliaia di loro significa in ogni caso tornare ad avere un appuntamento quotidiano, una lezione da seguire, dei compagni accanto e un luogo in cui continuare, o almeno tentare, a costruire il proprio futuro.
In mezzo alle macerie, alle tende e alle migliaia di difficoltà, la scuola prova così a tornare a essere quello che dovrebbe essere ovunque: uno spazio dove le bambine e i bambini possano imparare, immaginare e coltivare possibilità.
Anche quando l’aula è fatta di tela e legno. O quando il banco non c’è.

title: 50 jaar metro in Brussel: "Niet de beste in Europa, maar scoort zeker niet slecht"
content:
Op 20 september 1976, dag op dag 50 jaar geleden, werd in Brussel de eerste volwaardige metrolijn ingehuldigd. Dat was veel later dan in een reeks andere Europese steden, maar vandaag beschikt onze hoofdstad toch wel over een modern systeem van openbaar vervoer. Hoe is het metronetwerk tot stand gekomen en voldoet het aan de mobiliteitsnoden van de stad? 5 vragen en antwoorden.
50 jaar metro in Brussel: "Niet de beste in Europa, maar scoort zeker niet slecht"
Waarom pas in 1976 een metro?
De eerste plannen voor een metro in Brussel dateren al van het einde van de 19e eeuw. Koning-bouwheer Leopold II wilde niet onderdoen voor steden als Londen, Parijs en Boedapest, waar wel al ondergronds massatransport rondreed. Toch duurde het tot de jaren 50 van de vorige eeuw voor de eerste tunnel werd geopend in de buurt van het Zuidstation.
Dat het zo lang heeft geduurd, heeft zo zijn redenen. "Vergeet niet dat grote delen van het stadscentrum decennialang hebben opengelegen voor de bouw van de , wat een trauma heeft veroorzaakt", legt Stefan Stynen van reizigersvereniging uit. "Veel Brusselaars zagen hun stad liever niet nog een keer opengewoeld worden voor een metro."
De premetro toch wel een unieke en creatieve oplossing Stefan Stynen (TreinTramBus)
Stefan Stynen (TreinTramBus)
Ook de moerassige Brusselse ondergrond was een uitdaging voor de tunnelbouwers. "Op dat probleem botst men vandaag nog altijd", zegt Stynen. "Denk maar aan de moeilijkheden bij de bouw van metro 3." De aanleg van metrolijnen is een duur en complex project.
In de jaren 60 begon men toch te graven. Bij wijze van tussenstap werd gekozen voor een zogenoemde . "Toch wel een unieke en creatieve oplossing", vindt Stefan Stynen. "Financieel en praktisch was het gemakkelijker om trams ondergronds te laten rijden en zo meer ruimte te geven aan de auto. Op zich vind ik dat geen slechte werkwijze."
Het is wel zo dat Brussel in het verleden vaak voor de auto heeft gekozen. "Denk maar aan de tunnels op de Kleine Ring, op maat van het autoverkeer. Het is heel moeilijk om zoiets terug te draaien."
Waarom geen metro in het noorden en het zuiden?
Wie de kaart van het Brusselse metronetwerk bekijkt, ziet dat een groot deel van de noordelijke wijken en het zuiden van de stad niet wordt bediend.
Het was de bedoeling om de noordelijke gemeentes Schaarbeek en Evere met een nieuwe lijn aan te sluiten op het netwerk, maar door de rampzalige toestand van de openbare financiën van het Brusselse Gewest heeft de nieuwe Brusselse regering besloten om dat dure project af te voeren.
Ook in het zuiden van de stad rijdt geen metro. "In Ukkel wilde men dat destijds niet", weet Stefan Stynen. "Een deel van de lokale politici beschouwde openbaar vervoer als iets wat niet voor hen is. Zij gaven de voorkeur aan hun eigen auto."
Waarom geen metro in de randgemeenten?
Ook in de - Vlaamse - randgemeenten vind je geen metro. "Objectief beschouwd vind je in de weinig gebieden die voldoende dichtbevolkt zijn om de verlenging van een metrolijn te rechtvaardigen", zegt Stynen.
"De metro staat voor hen voor meer verstedelijking en . Er heerst een vrees voor 'verbrusseling', die geassocieerd wordt met de import van grootstedelijke problemen en criminaliteit. Dat laatste is onterecht, want criminelen rijden ook met de auto."
"Ook het model met pendelaars die hun auto achterlaten aan een park-and-ride aan de rand van de stad en de metro naar hun werk in het stadscentrum nemen, is niet realistisch. Dat zou betekenen dat je alleen metroreizigers hebt tijdens de spits, en dat is te weinig om de verlenging van een metrolijn te rechtvaardigen. Over zoiets moet je eerst een doordachte visie ontwikkelen."
Hoe veilig is de metro?
Als het over verkeersveiligheid gaat, is de Brusselse metro superveilig. Brussel heeft wel een veiligheidsprobleem in een aantal metrostations, maar dat heeft meer te maken met drugscriminaliteit en daklozenproblematiek. "Als er onveiligheid heerst op straat, zie je dat ook in de metro", denkt Stynen. "Poortjes in de metrostations houden dat niet tegen. De metro is een afspiegeling van wat je bovengronds ziet."
Het beleid van de overheid schiet hier tekort
Stefan Stynen (TreinTramBus)
Oplossingen liggen niet zo voor de hand. "Je moet mensen zien weg te leiden van drugs en tegen dealers moet je optreden. Wat in elk geval ook werkt, is de aanwezigheid van personeel in de metrostations."
Dat geldt in zekere zin ook voor de daklozenproblematiek. "Metrostations zijn niet geschikt als opvangplaats. Daklozen herbergen in ruimtes zonder sanitair of deftige eetplekken creëert een onveiligheidsgevoel, zelfs al doen die daklozen voor de rest niets fout. Het beleid van de overheid schiet hier tekort."
Wat kan beter?
Vandaag telt Brussel 4 metrolijnen en 69 metrostations, premetrostations inbegrepen. "Metro, trams en bussen samen bestrijken zowat de hele stad", weet Stefan Stynen. "Over het algemeen werkt dat wel: er is een goede frequentie en de reizigersinformatie is goed."
Misschien is het beter om de focus te leggen op het bovengrondse net
Stefan Stynen (TreinTramBus)
"De Brusselse metro is niet de beste van Europa, maar scoort zeker niet slecht." Stynen gelooft niet dat het metronetwerk in de nabije toekomst nog zal worden uitgebreid. "Ik vrees dat dit vandaag technisch en financieel niet haalbaar is. Misschien is het beter om de focus te leggen op het bovengrondse net."
Wel positief is dat de meeste metrostations toegankelijk zijn voor mensen met een beperking. "Dat is stukken beter dan in Parijs bijvoorbeeld, waar amper 10 procent van de stations toegankelijk is voor rolstoelgebruikers." Stynen betreurt wel dat er aanvankelijk voor gekozen is om geen liften in de stations te installeren. "Er werden afzonderlijke minibusjes voor rolstoelgebruikers ingezet. Maar vandaag de dag worden de oudere metrostations verbouwd en komen er wel liften. Al kost dat veel geld."
Kan het beter? Jazeker. De oudste metrostellen zijn aan vervanging toe - wat geleidelijk aan ook gebeurt - en de veiligheidsproblematiek kan beter worden aangepakt.
De integratie van de tarieven - of het gebrek daaraan - van de Brusselse , het Vlaamse De Lijn en het Waalse LeTEC is een ander pijnpunt. "Nochtans is dat een onmisbare voorwaarde om reizigers vlotter te laten overstappen van streekvervoer naar stadsvervoer", denkt Stefan Stynen.

title: Kela researcher on mental health gender gap: "the system reaches young women better"
content:
On Tuesday Yle News reported that women born in 1997 have received significantly more rehabilitative psychotherapy and sickness allowance than their male counterparts.
By their 28th birthday, 33.9 percent of women and 15.3 percent of men had received at least one of these benefits or rehabilitative psychotherapy, according to data compiled by Kela, the country's social insurance agency.
The gender gap was particularly striking in terms of rehabilitation psychotherapy: 15.9 percent of women had received it, compared to only 3.6 percent of men.
The country's mental health services system may not be adequately reaching young men, according to Kela's research chief Miika Vuori.
Vuori said the data shows that boys are referred to rehabilitation services earlier in life — in particular between ages 6-10. According to Kela's data, primary school-age boys are prescribed ADHD medication considerably more than girls.
"Research shows that psychological symptoms in girls and young women become more common during adolescence. Rehabilitation psychotherapy is only available from age 16, so the system reaches young women better," Vuori said.
He further noted that health service use is also linked to people's socioeconomic status — those in more difficult financial situations may have fewer opportunities to access rehabilitation psychotherapy.
Unknown factors
Diagnoses and treatment for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) have also increased among young girls over the past five years.
Earlier this year, it was reported that the number of children and young people in Finland being diagnosed with ADHD has continued to increase. Young boys tend to be more likely to receive an ADHD diagnosis, but the rate among girls aged 13-17 years old has also risen significantly in recent years.
"If we go back ten years, ADHD was hardly recognised in girls born in 1997. This shows that practices for seeking treatment and identifying service needs are changing," Vuori said.
Public health care has seen a significant increase in young people seeking mental health care. Vuori confirmed that mental health problems and neurodevelopmental syndromes are especially common in childhood and adolescence, and that the conditions affect their studying and work ability.
Kela's revelation about the data showed for the first time what percentage of an age group born in Finland accessed mental health benefits or rehabilitation psychotherapy between adolescence and early adulthood.
However, precise information about factors causing gender differences is not yet available.
"Such large differences between genders undeniably raise the question of whether something in our system or healthcare is partly producing these differences. This will be investigated in Kela's future research," Vuori said.

title: Vilniuje vyko unikalios žaidynės: tarp Tėvynės gynėjų – ir Lietuvos rinktinių nariai
content:
Penktadienį Vilniuje jau 13 kartą vyko Tėvynės gynėjų žaidynės, kuriose aštuoniose sporto šakose jėgas išbandė Lietuvos kariuomenės, policijos ir kitų valstybės saugumą bei viešąją tvarką užtikrinančių institucijų atstovai, rašoma pranešime žiniasklaidai.
Renginyje varžėsi daugiau nei 200 dalyvių, tarp kurių buvo ir Lietuvos vardą profesionalų varžybose garsinančių sportininkų.
Pagrindinis renginio tikslas – taikomųjų ir kitų sporto šakų populiarinimas tarp kariuomenės, policijos ir kitų statutinių institucijų, gerinant jų profesinį pasirengimą.
„Šis renginys turi gražią ir prasmingą tradiciją, tačiau jo esmė ne varžymasis, o žmonės, kurie savo kasdieniu darbu, tarnyba ir pasiryžimu prisideda prie Lietuvos saugumo. Žmonės, kurie skirtingose institucijose atlieka skirtingas užduotis, tačiau yra susieti vienu tikslu – saugoti tai, kas mums visiems yra brangu.
Tėvynės gynėjo vardas yra ne vien pareigybė ar uniforma, tai pirmiausia atsakomybė už savo valstybę, šalį, žmogų“, – atidarymo ceremonijoje varžybų dalyvius sveikino Lietuvos kariuomenės logistikos valdybos vadas pulkininkas Andrius Jagminas.
Daugiausiai čempionų titulų – penkis – iškovojo Lietuvos kariuomenės atstovai: vyrų tinklinio turnyro nugalėtojais tapo Darius Dūdėnas ir Adrijus Totoris, krepšinio 3x3 varžybas laimėjo Žydrūnas Bautronis, Tomas Sabaliauskas, Dovydas Lisauskas ir Benediktas Petraška, šachmatų – Pijus Greičius ir kariuomenės komanda, o estafetinio bėgimo – Rytis Ašmena, Lukas Šermukšnis, Teklė Emilija Gvildytė ir Viktorija Varnagirytė.
T. E. Gvildytė – viena pajėgiausių Lietuvos orientavimosi sporto atstovių, tuo tarpu L. Šermukšnis ir V. Varnagirytė yra daugkartiniai Lietuvos lengvosios atletikos čempionai.
„Pati varžybų pradžia mane nustebino, nes teko vytis varžovę: praėjusiais metais kaip išbėgau pirma, taip ir finišavau. Mačiau, kad varžovė lėtėja, tai pasistengiau ir pavyko perduoti lazdelę pirmai, – pasakojo V. Varnagirytė. – Pastaraisiais metais kaip Lietuvos kariuomenės atstovė vykau į kelerias tarptautines varžybas, o dalyvavimas jose davė daug patirties – esu labai dėkinga. Seniau teko atstovauti ir Lietuvos rinktinei, o dabar mano tikslas mėgautis bėgimu. Kai pradėjau tą daryti, pradėjo ir vėl sektis.“
Moterų tinklinio turnyre pirmąją vietą iškovojo Finansinių nusikaltimų tyrimo tarnybos komanda, kuriai atstovavo Laura Bagdonaitė ir Miglė Murauskaitė. Mažojo futbolo varžybose triumfavo Priešgaisrinės apsaugos ir gelbėjimo departamento ekipa, o stalo tenise – Lietuvos policijos atstovai.
Šaudymo iš tarnybinio ginklo rungtyje taikliausia buvo Vadovybės apsaugos tarnybos trijulė (Miroslavas Nedveckij, Povilas Vaskinas, Arvydas Vaitekūnas), asmeninėje šios rungties įskaitoje triumfavo A. Vaitiekūnas, o šaudymo iš pistoleto varžybas tarp vadovybės atstovų laimėjo Giedrius Geniušas (Valstybės sienos apsaugos tarnyba).
„Dalyvauju ne pirmą kartą, varžybos labai svarbios, manau, kad jos suvienija visas tarnybas ir, svarbiausia, leidžia pabendrauti vieniems su kitais. Tikiuosi, kad varžybos stiprės ir bus vis reikšmingesnės. Ar nebuvo jaudulio šaudant? Mes pareigūnai ir nuolat treniruojamės, tad jaudulio nebuvo. Prieš tai pasidarėme treniruotę, pasibandėme ir viskas puikiai sekėsi“, – komentavo G. Geniušas.
Pirmosios Lietuvos kariuomenės ir policijos žaidynės vyko dar 2009 metais. Po ketverių metų šis renginys buvo pervadintas į Tėvynės gynėjų žaidynes, o varžytis jose buvo pakviesti ir kitų statutinių įstaigų pareigūnai.

title: Ukraine's Skelia Regiment evacuates 21 soldiers from encirclement
content:
Ukraine's Skelia Regiment evacuates 21 soldiers from encirclement
Ukrainian fighters from the Skelia unit – the 425th Assault Regiment – have evacuated 21 soldiers from the 159th Brigade who had spent more than 10 months on the front line without rotation.
Source: a video by the 425th Assault Regiment
Quote: "For more than 10 months, servicemen from the 159th Separate Mechanised Brigade had been stationed on the front line without rotation. Eventually, they found themselves surrounded, and leaving the area on their own was practically impossible.
The command of the 425th Skelia Assault Regiment planned and carried out a combat operation to evacuate the servicemen from the 159th Brigade."
Details: The Skelia fighters had to engage in combat and clear a route to rescue their brothers-in-arms, allowing groups of the 159th Brigade to escape the encirclement.
As a result, 21 servicemen were evacuated from the combat zone.
During the assault, the fighters destroyed Russian positions and captured several Russian soldiers.

title: Travelling with dementia
content:
When Dr Debra Graves OAM boarded a cruise ship, it wasn’t uncommon for her to wedge suitcases against her cabin door before going to sleep.
It wasn’t because she was worried about intruders. It was to help prevent her husband Don — who was living with dementia — from waking during the night and wandering from their cabin.
It was just one of many practical strategies Debra developed to ensure she and Don could continue travelling after his dementia diagnosis.
Despite the challenges that came with caring for someone living with dementia, Debra says continuing to travel remained a priority because it brought them both immense joy.
Even as Don’s condition progressed, the couple continued to travel — something Debra admits required extensive preparation to ensure everything went as smoothly as possible.
“Travelling with Don at that point in his life involved next-level preparation,” she says.
“But I had it down pat because we travelled a lot.”
As the couple had always enjoyed cruising holidays, Debra developed some practical safety strategies that allowed them to continue going on cruises together.
“I would use extra suitcases to barricade the cabin door at night as a form of protection in case Don got up and wandered,” she says. “If the sensor mat didn’t wake me, I thought the sound of the suitcases would.”
Travel helped keep Don stimulated, engaged and improved his quality of life
An avid cruiser, Debra says Don felt comfortable out on the water, and particularly enjoyed spending time on deck.
“If we hadn’t continued to travel, I think Don’s condition would have deteriorated faster,” she says.
“Travel helped keep Don stimulated, engaged, and improved his quality of life.”
Just as importantly, Debra says travelling helped the couple maintain their connection while enjoying something that had long been a familiar part of their life together.
With more than 446,000 Australians living with dementia — and an estimated 1.7 million people involved in their care — Debra hopes more people realise a diagnosis doesn’t necessarily have to mean the end of travel, provided there is someone willing to adapt, plan ahead, and offer the right support.
“Of course, travelling with dementia isn’t always easy,” Debra says.
“We had to adapt, and we had to think ahead. But we also had wonderful experiences together. I would never want families to feel that a diagnosis means they have to immediately cancel the things that bring them joy.
“Dementia may change the way you travel. It doesn’t necessarily mean the journey has to end.”
Practical travel advice from one carer to another
With Dementia Action Week running from September 21-27, Debra hopes her experience will encourage more conversations about not only the challenges of dementia, but also the things people living with the condition can continue to enjoy.
“Every journey is different,” she says. “There is no single right way to travel when supporting someone living with dementia. What matters is finding what works for you and the person you are supporting.”
Debra says she would also like to see more conversations focus on what remains possible after a diagnosis.
“I think we need to talk about all of it, including the things people living with dementia still want to do and have always enjoyed,” she says.
“Travel is one of those things. Too often, the conversation starts with what someone can no longer do. I’d much rather we started asking what is still possible, and what would make it possible for more people.”
To help those caring for and supporting someone living with dementia, Debra has put together a list of practical travel tips she found useful when travelling with her husband Don after his diagnosis.
+ Maintain familiar routines wherever possible.
+ Plan a slower-paced trip with built-in rest periods.
+ Avoid over-scheduling activities.
+ Choose quieter travel times and less crowded destinations where possible.
+ Use clear, simple communication.
+ Prepare for fatigue and behavioural changes.
+ Pack a dedicated travel kit with medications, clothing, and comfort items.
+ Carry identification and emergency contact details at all times.
+ Choose direct transport routes where possible.
+ Allow extra time for boarding, transfers, and delays.
+ Notify airlines and transport providers in advance of assistance needs.
+ Select quiet, secure accommodation that is easy to navigate.
+ Avoid frequent changes in accommodation or complex itineraries.
+ Ensure access to nearby healthcare services.
Debra shares more of her experience and deeply personal stories in her book To Dementia With Love, co-written with Jane Carstens, which is available via Amazon, The Book Adviser, the National Library of Australia Bookshop (Canberra) and The Burns Bay Bookery (Lane Cove, Sydney).

title: After stroke at 38, UAE-based mother starts initiative to help women rebuild
content:
After stroke at 38, UAE-based mother starts initiative to help women rebuild
Rucha Daryani says the hardest part of recovery began when others assumed she was well again
- PUBLISHED: Thu 24 Sept 2026, 11:50 AM
Before April 2024, Rucha Daryani’s days were filled with school runs, two young children and workshops for women trying to reconnect with themselves. At 38, she was building The Mum Identity Project and thinking about what she wanted to do next.
A stroke was nowhere in those plans.
“I had a clear sense of who I was and what I was doing, and I had never once considered that a stroke was something that could happen to me at 38,” she told Khaleej Times.
Daryani had gone to hospital because her ferritin, a measure of the body’s iron stores, was low. She said a doctor recommended an iron infusion, a treatment she had received before but had not tolerated well. She raised her concerns and explained that her previous infusions had been administered slowly. This one, she said, was given much faster.
Partway through, she felt something was wrong and sent her husband to find the doctor. “That's the last thing I remember,” she said.
Her next memory is of waking in a neuro ICU. Her husband was asking whether she recognised him, whether she knew they had children and whether she could name them. She has no memory of the time between those moments.
In the weeks that followed, Daryani said she had little space to process what had happened. Her attention was on her children and the next task in front of her.
“There was no moment of taking it all in, no sitting with the enormity of what had happened. You don't have room for that. You're just surviving,” she said.
Her account raises a question she continues to think about: what happens when a woman says something is wrong with her body and feels she has not been heard?
Daryani said there was no formal review or investigation into her treatment. Her family decided against pursuing one while she was recovering and caring for two young children.
She does not name the hospital or doctor, and the circumstances leading to her stroke have not been independently established.
“I had a recovery ahead of me, two small children, and a finite amount of energy, and I had to choose where it went. I chose the rebuilding,” she said.
That experience has shaped The Second Act, a UAE-based initiative Daryani plans to launch publicly in October for women navigating major changes in their lives. Its focus extends beyond illness to experiences such as motherhood, divorce, burnout and career disruption.
For Daryani, recovery was about more than regaining physical abilities. It also meant facing the period after the immediate crisis, when she appeared well to others but was still adjusting to a life that had changed.
The Second Act grew from her belief that women need room to rebuild at their own pace, without being expected to return to who they were before.
“We celebrate survival, but often expect people to return to who they were before,” she said in background material shared with Khaleej Times. “You don't go back, you build forward.”
Daryani is also preparing to release The Light Never Left, a children’s picture book inspired by her family’s experience of stroke and recovery. Both the book and The Second Act are expected to launch in October.
For now, she hopes her story opens a conversation about the part of recovery that is harder to see, and about listening when women speak up about their health.
“I said something was wrong and I wasn't listened to,” she said. “That's the piece I think is worth everyone's attention.”

title: Završena je treća Helem Nejse Talent Akademija u Sarajevu: Učestvovalo 40 mladih kreativaca iz regije
content:
Završena je treća Helem Nejse Talent Akademija u Sarajevu: Učestvovalo 40 mladih kreativaca iz regije
Nakon ceremonije uslijedio je closing party otvoren za javnost. Na DJ pultu su se smjenjivali Toshi kao domaćin, Phat Phillie i Lord Finesse, legendarni njujorški producent koji je istog popodneva održao i radionicu beatmakinga s polaznicima Akademije.
Četrdeset polaznika i polaznica iz Bosne i Hercegovine, Srbije, Hrvatske, Crne Gore, Slovenije i Sjeverne Makedonije kroz tri dana prošlo je intenzivan program iz oblasti muzičke produkcije, grafičkog dizajna i animacije te kreativne produkcije, uz više od 20 predavača iz cijele regije i svijeta.
"Toliko je lijepo biti okružena ljudima koji imaju inspirativne priče kako je nešto uspjelo. Bavili smo se
malo i time kako je teško stanje u kulturi i kako se borimo sa tim, ali opet, najsnažniji utisak mi je strast koju ljudi ovdje imaju, koja se prenosi na sve nas. Već smo pričali i dogovaramo buduće projekte na kojima ćemo sarađivati, i mislim da je to nekako najveća vrijednost, i da je zapravo i cilj ove akademije na neki način to povezivanje mladih kreativaca iz naše regije", kazala je Ana Ćulum, polaznica programa Kreativna produkcija koja dolazi iz Zagreba.
Akademija je počela u četvrtak naveče kino premijerom dugometražnog animiranog filma "Bruca Braca Bruda Brada — Zombi apokalipsa" i Masterclassom s autorskim timom filma. Tokom tri dana, polaznici su radili na više lokacija u Sarajevu, sa više od 20 predavača koji dolaze iz cijele regije, uz nekoliko svjetskih imena.
Program Primijenjene muzičke produkcije vodio je polaznike kroz vokalnu produkciju, mixing, elektronsku muziku za savremene medije, AI u muzičkoj produkciji, beatmaking, songwriting i DJ kulturu, te organizaciju muzičkih festivala. Među predavačima su bili Grammy nominirani inženjer Damjan Blažun, legendarni njujorški producent Lord Finesse, dobitnik Emmy nagrade dr. Mladen Milićević, Phat Phillie, Indigo i Toshi Domaćin.
"Ako sam danas svojom pričom dotakao nekoga od ovih mladih ljudi, i ako će jednog dana biti sjajni u onome što rade, a ja čujem da sam imao uticaj na to — to me čini sretnim. Znati da sam imao svrhu koja je veća od mojih ciljeva i ambicija", poručio je Lord Finesse.
Program Grafičkog dizajna i animacije pokrivao je tipografiju, dizajn postera, ilustraciju, JUS dizajn i
animaciju karaktera, a predavali su Haris Jusović, Marko i Darko Miladinović, Vanesa Durmišević i Mladen Đukić.
Program Kreativne produkcije vodio je polaznike kroz različite strane produkcijskog procesa — od pozorišne produkcije s direktorom Kamernog teatra 55 Vedranom Fajkovićem i pozorišnih festivala s Miroslavom Radonjićem iz Sterijinog pozorja, preko case studyja knjige i predstave "Blank" s Feđom Štukanom i radionice pitchinga s Rifatom Rifatovićem, do case studyja organizacije Sarajevo Film
Festivala s Arminom Hadžićem u Meeting Pointu i analize produkcije serije "Kotlina" s producenticom Amrom Bakšić Čamo.
Zajednički program Kritičkog mišljenja ponudio je panel o kulturi u kreativnoj ekonomiji sa Sinišom Šešumom, predstavnikom UNESCO-a u BiH, te FEMIX sesiju o jednakosti i vidljivosti u kreativnim industrijama s Anom Janković i Katarinom Zarić.
Helem Nejse Talent Akademija organizuje se u sklopu projekta koji finansira Vlada Ujedinjenog Kraljevstva kroz UK International Development.

title: Allahabad High Court asks UP police to ensure safety for same-sex interfaith couple
content:
5 min readNew DelhiSep 21, 2026 04:30 PM IST

The Allahabad High Court has granted protection to two adult women from different faiths in a same-sex live-in relationship, holding that they have the right to live together peacefully. The court directed the police to provide them protection if anyone threatens or interferes with their life or liberty.
Justice Dr Gautam Chowdhary was hearing a petition filed by the two women who told the court that both were adults, unmarried and living together. They alleged that their family members and others were interfering with their peaceful life and threatening and harassing them. Both women appeared personally before the court after an earlier order dated September 10 directed them to remain present.
“The petitioners are fully protected under Article 21. The petitioners are adults, are homosexual, are educated and are fully capable of understanding what is in their own interest. They have decided, after due consideration, to live together and no one has exercised any force or coercion upon them. Therefore, no one has any right to oppose the petitioners living together in a live-in relationship, and this court finds no reason to refuse their prayer for protection. The present petition deserves to be allowed,” the court said on September 14.




The ruling followed the court’s personal interaction with both women. It recorded that they were adults, capable of understanding what was in their own interest and had chosen to live together voluntarily. Both said they wanted to continue living together and had taken the decision without pressure, fear or undue influence.
Justice Dr Gautam Chowdhary personally interacted with the two women and found that their decision to live together was based on free consent. (Image enhanced using AI)
Women sought protection
The petitioners’ counsel informed the court that both women were adults and produced copies of their high-school marksheets to establish their ages. They were unmarried and said they were in a live-in relationship.
They alleged that their family members were unhappy with their relationship and that they faced threats and harassment following which, they approached the high court under seeking directions to police authorities to protect their lives and prevent interference with their relationship.
Their counsel argued that the choice of an adult to live with a partner forms part of personal autonomy, dignity and privacy protected by the Constitution. The state’s counsel submitted that while a person’s choice of partner is protected under Article 21, legislative recognition of such a relationship is not itself a fundamental right. The state also referred to the lack of social acceptance of same-sex relationships and traditional views surrounding marriage and family.
Story continues below this ad
Court verified their decision
The high court did not decide the petition solely on the lawyers’ submissions. Both the women appeared before the judge and said they were adults and had decided of their own free will to live together because of their same-sex relationship.
They also told the court that they wanted to continue living together. After personally interviewing them, the court recorded that both were adults, capable of understanding what was in their own interest and that their decision was based on free consent. Both women submitted written statements saying that they were in same-sex relationship and living together.
Court separates right to live together from marriage
The high court considered Supreme Court rulings concerning the rights and legal position of queer and LGBTQ+ persons. It referred to the Supreme Court’s earlier ruling recognising sexual orientation as an aspect of freedom, dignity, privacy and individual autonomy.
Considering the Supreme Court’s later ruling that there is no unqualified right to marriage except where recognised by statute or custom, it said that the Supreme Court had also held that legal recognition of a union similar to marriage or a civil union could be created only through legislation. At the same time, it recognised that queer and LGBTQ+ couples have a right to form relationships or unions under Article 21, flowing from privacy, choice and autonomy.
Story continues below this ad
Taking note of this legal position, the court said the absence of legal recognition of same-sex marriage did not remove the constitutional protection available to two consenting adults who choose to live together. It said such relationships are protected under Article 21 through privacy, choice and personal autonomy.
The court said that if their peaceful life was disturbed, the women could approach the concerned police commissioner, senior superintendent of police or superintendent of police with a certified copy of the order. After verifying that they were adults and voluntarily living together, the police were directed to provide them immediate protection.

title: Côte d’Ivoire-AIP/ L’ambassadrice du Canada visite des infrastructures sociales réalisées à Togonieré avec l’appui de son pays
content:
Ferkessédougou, 18 sept 2026 (AIP) – L’ambassadrice du Canada en Côte d’Ivoire, Sandra Choufany, a visité mercredi 16 septembre 2026, des infrastructures sociales réalisées au centre de santé urbain (CSU) de Togonieré, dans le département de Ferkessédougou, avec l’appui financier du Canada.
La visite s’est déroulée en présence de représentants du Fonds des Nations unies pour la population (UNFPA), de l’ONG Action contre la faim (ACF) et de l’UNICEF, ainsi que du corps préfectoral, des autorités sanitaires, des cadres et des populations de la localité.
Le médecin-chef du CSU de Togonieré, Dr Siagbé Soumgolé, a expliqué que ces infrastructures, réalisées par l’ACF grâce au financement canadien, ont permis d’améliorer les conditions d’accueil et de prise en charge des patients.
Selon lui, elles offrent désormais aux usagers un cadre de soins plus adapté, moderne et sécurisé, tout en améliorant les conditions de travail du personnel soignant. Il a assuré que les équipements et infrastructures sont utilisés au bénéfice de la communauté.
La vice-présidente de la mutuelle de développement de Togonieré, Koné Blandine, a exprimé la satisfaction des populations et des cadres de la localité, saluant l’appui régulier du Canada aux initiatives sociales dans le canton Palaka et le département de Ferkessédougou.
Sandra Choufany s’est réjouie de constater l’impact de ces réalisations sur les populations. Elle a salué les relations entre la Côte d’Ivoire et le Canada et assuré que les investissements destinés à renforcer la résilience des populations de la région du Tchologo se poursuivront.
Le sous-préfet de Koumbala, Firmin Gompeu, assurant l’intérim de son homologue de Togonieré, a salué cette visite et la contribution du Canada à plusieurs projets et initiatives sociales dans la localité.
La délégation a également échangé avec les autorités locales et les bénéficiaires sur l’utilisation des infrastructures et les besoins de la communauté.

title: Second-life PV modules turned into solar balconies in Germany
content:
Second-life PV modules turned into solar balconies in Germany
A photovoltaic reuse initiative in Kassel, Germany, has repurposed 300 used solar modules to create 150 balcony PV systems.
The panels, which had operated for 13 years on the roof of an industrial building, were inspected, refurbished and distributed to participants in an upcycling project organized by ClimateHub Kassel and solar collective SoLocal Energy.
The project began with inspections of the 300 recovered modules. Twelve panels showed minor defects and were discarded, while the remaining modules were cleaned and fitted with new connectors for use in balcony PV systems. The recovered modules represent around 6 metric tons of material that would otherwise have entered recycling streams, where only certain material fractions can be recovered.
The organizers introduced a tiered pricing model to make the systems accessible to households with different budgets. Complete packages include modules, an inverter, mounting equipment, cabling and accessories, as well as electrical connection, system registration and monitoring setup.
A system comprising two 325 W CSW Excellent modules, for a total capacity of 650 W, costs €825 ($937) under the subsidized tariff, €1,000 at the standard rate and €1,175 under the solidarity tariff. A single-module system costs €650, €775 and €900, respectively. A four-module configuration using CSW Diamond panels has a combined capacity of 1.78 kW and costs €2,025 under the highest pricing tier specified by the organizers.
Participants can also collect the equipment and install the systems themselves. Two-module systems are supplied with a Hoymiles HMS-800W-2T microinverter. Three- and four-module systems use either two SUN-M80 units or one Hoymiles HMS-1600-4WB inverter, with dynamic power control limiting total output to 800 W.
An optional storage package, comprising a Zendure SolarFlow 800 Pro 2 battery and an energy meter, costs an additional €600 to €700, depending on the pricing tier. Professional-grade modules are also available for €30 more per panel than the Diamond modules.
Several local organizations provided logistical and technical support. Bauteilbörse handled 13 pallets of modules, while BürgerSolarBeratung and energy cooperative Bürgerenergiegenossenschaft Kassel & Söhre provided technical assistance. Cargo bikes were made available to help participants transport the modules.
German nonprofit organization Deutsche Gesellschaft für Sonnenenergie (DGS) also made a donation to reduce the cost of inverters and mounting equipment for some low-income households.

title: Filha surpreende pai com a primeira festa de aniversário da vida dele, aos 73 anos; vídeo
content:
Filha surpreende pai com a primeira festa de aniversário da vida dele, aos 73 anos; vídeo
Aos 73 anos, o seu Lewis finalmente teve uma comemoração que nunca havia vivido. A filha, Daija, de 28, organizou secretamente a primeira festa de aniversário do pai e reuniu amigos e colegas de trabalho para surpreendê-lo em Maryland, nos Estados Unidos.
O idoso nunca teve uma festa de aniversário na vida e quando Daija descobriu isso, ela decidiu preparar uma celebração completa e passou quase dois meses entrando em contato com pessoas importantes na vida dele.
Ao chegar e encontrar todos reunidos para festejar seus 73 anos, Lewis Freeman não acreditou na quantidade de gente que havia participado do plano. Para ele, ver amigos e colegas juntos foi uma das partes mais especiais do presente.
Surpresa levou quase dois meses
Daija manteve os preparativos em segredo para que o pai não desconfiasse. Durante semanas, ela procurou amigos e colegas de trabalho de Lewis para reunir as pessoas que fizeram parte da trajetória dele.
A intenção era mostrar o quanto ele é amado por todos. E deu certo.
Lewis descreveu a comemoração como a “melhor surpresa” e contou que significou muito ver tantas pessoas reunidas para celebrar com ele.

title: Baixo financiamento e fechamento de unidades: o SUS faz milagres em MG
content:
O Sistema Único de Saúde Brasileiro (SUS) é, segundo a Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU), referência internacional na área de saúde pública. Por sua vez, o Banco Mundial, que publicou o livro 20 anos de Construção do SUS no Brasil, afirma que: “com base nessa experiência e apesar de todas as dificuldades inerentes a um país em desenvolvimento, o Brasil é referência internacional na área de saúde pública e exemplo para outros países que buscam sistemas mais igualitários de saúde”.
Internacionalmente reconhecido como uma das propostas mais bem-sucedidas na área, o sistema ainda é subfinanciado. Os dados mais recentes apontam que a rede pública de saúde brasileira é composta por 301 mil agentes comunitários de saúde, mais de 55 mil equipes de Saúde da Família, 76 mil unidades ambulatoriais, 7,2 mil unidades hospitalares e 313 mil leitos.
Apesar da proporção, de acordo com dados da Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS), em comparativo com outros países que se propõem a universalizar o acesso público à saúde, o Brasil apresenta baixíssimos investimentos per capita. O país gasta 610 dólares anualmente, enquanto França, Reino Unido, Canadá, Austrália, Portugal, Espanha e Itália, investem mais de 2 mil dólares por cidadão em um ano (Média de 2021), o que equivale a entre 8 e 10% de seu Produto Interno Bruto (PIB). Sendo que os dois primeiros direcionam mais de 4 mil per capita para a manutenção da saúde.
Como funciona o financiamento do SUS?
O financiamento público deste sistema de dimensões continentais equivale a 3,9% do PIB brasileiro (2023). A gestão é feita a partir do sistema tripartite no qual União, estados e municípios compartilham responsabilidades no financiamento e na execução das ações de saúde.
A União, esfera federal, é responsável por repasses nacionais e políticas estratégicas; já os estados coordenam a rede regional de saúde e apoiam os municípios que, por sua vez, são responsáveis pela execução direta da maior parte dos serviços, como atendimento nas unidades de saúde.
Porém, como o repasse acontece por meio de transferências chamadas de “fundo a fundo”, o Governo do Estado exerce papel central na organização e distribuição dos recursos. É ele que coordena a rede regional de saúde e garante o apoio necessário para a execução dos atendimentos no SUS.
Cenário em MG
Em Minas Gerais, a situação de precarização do SUS se tornou uma realidade grave nós últimos anos. De acordo com pesquisa Quaest, divulgada no final de julho, a saúde está entre as áreas que mais preocupam os mineiros nas eleições de 2026. Para 32% dos consultados, a atuação do executivo estadual na saúde é negativa, enquanto 38% a consideram apenas regular.
A frente do estado por dois mandatos, desde 2018, a política de Romeu Zema (Novo) é vista por críticos como uma asfixia do SUS na intenção de vender a “solução” privada como única saída. Enquanto outdoors espalhados pelo estado alardeiam uma “saúde que avança”, a realidade vivida pela população e pelos servidores da área revela um projeto político de desmonte, privatização e desrespeito aos direitos básicos.
É o que apontou, em entrevista ao Brasil de Fato MG, o médico infectologista e professor da Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (UFMG) Unaí Tupinambás.
“Infelizmente, a gente não tem muito o que comemorar nesses oito anos do governo Zema. Três características marcam esse período: a omissão, a incompetência e a burocratização. Vê-se que é uma situação catastrófica”, resume o médico.
Atraso nas entregas e fechamento de unidades
Um dos gargalos mais críticos, a falta de hospitais que atendem regionalmente casos de alta complexidade obriga os mineiros e mineiras das diversas regiões no interior do estado a viajarem horas para conseguir atendimento na capital, sobrecarregando o sistema de Belo Horizonte, que também tem sofrido tentativas de encolhimento.
Apesar da busca do governo estadual, hoje comandado por Mateus Simões (PSD), de vender a ideia de conclusão dos hospitais regionais, os números não mentem. Das seis grandes unidades prometidas na campanha de 2018, em Sete Lagoas, Conselheiro Lafaiete, Teófilo Otoni, Governador Valadares, Divinópolis e Juiz de Fora, apenas duas foram entregues até março de 2026. Mesmo estas “entregas” merecem questionamento, tendo sido possibilitadas através de parcerias com a União e concessões à iniciativa privada, por meio da filantropia.
O hospital regional de Teófilo Otoni, “inaugurado” com atraso por Simões em 18 de junho, até o momento só está operando com a realização dos exames de imagem. O caso ganhou repercussão após a proposta de federalização do hospital ser defendida pelo vereador da cidade João Gabriel Prates (PT) nas redes sociais.
A proposta visa garantir sua plena abertura e funcionamento, diante da preocupação que o prédio permaneça pronto, mas sem capacidade operacional, sobretudo frente ao atual estado das finanças públicas. Localizado na cidade polo dos Vales do Mucuri e Jequitinhonha, o hospital atenderá o maior vazio assistencial de Minas.
“Não é só facilitar a vida, mas salvar vidas. Transferir um paciente do Norte de Minas para Belo Horizonte pode ser uma questão de vida ou morte. Se ele tem um hospital regionalizado, bem equipado e montado, é a diferença entre a vida e a morte daquele caso. Nós temos que estar atentos a essa descentralização, fortalecendo as regionais de saúde de Minas Gerais, criando autonomia, dando recursos e entregando o que foi prometido” denuncia Tupinambás.
Fechamento de hospitais e desvalorização dos servidores
Outra proposta controversa foi o plano de fechamento de unidades estratégicas da rede Fundação Hospitalar do Estado de Minas Gerais (Fhemig). Como explica Tupinambás, sob a justificativa de “modernização” e transferência para um novo complexo hospitalar (HoPE), o projeto de Zema pôs na mira o Hospital Maria Amélia Lins (HMAL), referência em ortopedia, e o Hospital Alberto Cavalcanti (HMAC), especializado em oncologia. Para especialistas, a iniciativa apenas mascara uma política de privatização via Organizações Sociais (OSs).
“O governo Zema propôs fechar esses hospitais e criar um hospital só. Mas o hospital sequer saiu do projeto e não tem nenhuma perspectiva. Você diminui o leito nesses hospitais em meio a uma tragédia que é não ter leitos para cirurgia ortopédica, sobrecarregando outras unidades. A fila para cirurgia, aí estou falando de cirurgia ortopédica, só faz aumentar.”, explica o professor da UFMG.
O Brasil de Fato MG acompanhou diversas manifestações de servidores e usuários que denunciam o risco de perda de leitos e a precarização do atendimento especializado. Estes mesmos servidores também denunciam perdas históricas. Isso porque, durante os sete anos de gestão Zema — dentre os quais os anos de pandemia, que exigiram trabalhos ainda maiores na saúde —, os servidores da área enfrentaram um arrocho salarial, com perdas inflacionárias que chegam a 27%.
“Temos que pensar a política de valorização do trabalhador. A gente não tem concurso público, você vai ver: é contrato. As pessoas têm alta rotatividade, e, claro, não têm vínculo porque têm um contrato de trabalho muito precarizado. É a uberização do trabalho da saúde”, complementa Tupinambás.

title: Phim về cô giáo tiếng Anh của trẻ vùng quê thắng giải 'Hiền tài hôm nay'

Phim về cô giáo tiếng Anh của trẻ vùng quê thắng giải 'Hiền tài hôm nay'
Hà NộiPhim ''Khát vọng vươn xa'' về nỗ lực của cô giáo tiếng Anh dạy ngoại ngữ cho trẻ nông thôn, đoạt giải nhất cuộc thi ''Hiền tài hôm nay''.
Tác phẩm được vinh danh tại lễ tổng kết và trao giải tại rạp Ngọc Khánh, tối 17/9. Phim do Hoàng Hà Lê đạo diễn, Bùi Thị Thoa biên kịch, Công ty TNHH MTV Hãng phim Tài liệu và Khoa học Trung ương sản xuất.
Khát vọng vươn xa kể về cô giáo Trần Thị Thúy tại THPT Đức Hợp, Hưng Yên. Do từng trải qua cảnh thiếu thốn cơ hội học tiếng Anh, cô xây dựng cách dạy kết hợp kiến thức bộ môn, phương pháp, công nghệ, sử dụng Skype, Wiki và các nền tảng trực tuyến để kết nối học sinh nông thôn với bạn bè quốc tế. Những chuyến "đi và đến'' 21 quốc gia qua màn hình và việc cô vào Top 50 Giáo viên toàn cầu đã tiếp thêm động lực cho học sinh vùng quê. Song hành giáo viên trẻ là người cha, dù vất vả mưu sinh, ông quyết tâm cho con theo đuổi học hành.
Đạo diễn Hoàng Hà Lê bất ngờ, hạnh phúc khi nhận giải cao nhất của cuộc thi. Cô thực hiện dự án năm 2021, thời điểm Covid-19 căng thẳng. Quá trình làm phim, điều thuận lợi là nhân vật cởi mở, tạo cơ hội để êkíp đào sâu hơn vào câu chuyện. Trong tác phẩm xuất hiện câu nói: ''Chỉ có học mới thành người''. Theo đạo diễn, có lẽ điều này đúng với tiêu chí thi và chạm đến cảm xúc của người xem, giúp cô đoạt giải nhất.
Hoàng Hà Lê 36 tuổi, sinh ở Hà Nội, công tác tại Hãng phim Tài liệu Khoa học Trung ương, theo đuổi các đề tài văn hóa, xã hội và con người Việt Nam. Một số tác phẩm tiêu biểu của cô gồm: Nhật ký của Ba, Làng xây đảo, Phía sau ánh hào quang, Kháng thuốc kháng sinh. Trong đó, Nhật ký của Ba từng giành Cánh diều Bạc phim tài liệu.
Ban tổ chức trao hai giải nhì, mỗi giải 30 triệu đồng cho phim tài liệu Chuyện một nữ trí thức Hà Nội (Đỗ Thị Huyền Trang), phim hoạt hình POOCBAGA (Trần Xuân Du).
Giải ba, mỗi giải 20 triệu đồng dành cho tác phẩm hoạt hình Sắc màu của núi (NSƯT Phùng Văn Hà), phim truyện Buổi lễ trưởng thành của ADEI (Cham Production), tác phẩm tài liệu Chạm vào tri thức (Lan Chi và Thảo Phan).
Giải khuyến khích nhận 10 triệu đồng mỗi giải thuộc về năm phim tài liệu: Người giữ lửa - Hành trình kết nối tri thức trên nền tảng số (nhóm tác giả On Record), Người thầy trước những vi rút tử thần (Vũ Thị Thu Hiền), Nghề/Nghiệp (Đỗ Trang Hà), Muôn đời đạo học (Đào Duy Từ), Nhìn là thấy Việt Nam (AVG).
Phim tài liệu Học của Phạm Nguyễn Phú Sĩ thắng hạng mục Phim được yêu thích nhất. Giải Ý tưởng sáng tạo được trao cho phim truyện Trưởng bản ngày mai của Lò Thanh Thanh. Mỗi tác giả nhận mức tiền thưởng 10 triệu đồng.
Trong đó, Học là tác phẩm đầu tay của Phạm Nguyễn Phú Sĩ, 24 tuổi, hiện học Thạc sĩ ngành Kỹ thuật Điện tử, trường Đại học Công nghệ, Đại học Quốc gia Hà Nội. Phim nhìn lại hành trình học tập lâu dài, bền bỉ của người Việt, như một ''ngọn lửa'' được thắp lên từ Văn Miếu - Quốc Tử Giám. Từ quan niệm học để thành đạt và giúp ích cho người, tinh thần ấy thích nghi qua chiến tranh và hòa bình, là sức mạnh để bảo vệ đất nước, mở rộng tâm hồn và đối thoại với thế giới.
Tiến sĩ Ngô Phương Lan - Chủ tịch Hiệp hội Xúc tiến phát triển Điện ảnh Việt Nam, đồng Trưởng ban tổ chức - cho biết sau hơn bốn tháng triển khai, ban tổ chức chọn được 23 phim vào vòng chung khảo trong hơn 200 tác phẩm.
Qua các phim dự thi, bà Ngô Phương Lan nhận thấy chủ đề hiền tài không bị đóng khung trong những bài học của quá khứ. Các tác giả đã tìm thấy hiền tài từ nhiều không gian của đời sống, ở lớp học, phòng nghiên cứu, trong nghệ thuật truyền thống, vùng núi hay giữa nhịp sống đô thị.
Tiến sĩ đánh giá những tác phẩm thắng giải tạo được sự hài hòa giữa câu chuyện ý nghĩa và cách thể hiện thuyết phục. Một số phim trong vòng chung khảo có đề tài tốt nhưng chưa tìm được cách kể điện ảnh, còn phụ thuộc vào lời bình phỏng vấn hoặc cách thể hiện mang tính minh họa. Điều này cho thấy việc làm phim là một chặng đường dài trau dồi, tích lũy kinh nghiệm, chất liệu. ''Tôi đặc biệt trân trọng nguồn năng lượng của các tác giả trẻ'', bà nói.
Cuộc thi phim ngắn Hiền tài hôm nay là một trong những hoạt động văn hóa trọng điểm hướng tới kỷ niệm 950 năm Quốc Tử Giám (1076-2026). Giải quy tụ nhiều thế hệ và thành phần sáng tác, từ những đơn vị điện ảnh chuyên nghiệp, các nghệ sĩ nhiều kinh nghiệm đến sinh viên, các nhóm làm phim độc lập và người trẻ lần đầu thử sức điện ảnh.
Sân chơi do Trung tâm Hoạt động Văn hóa Khoa học Văn Miếu - Quốc Tử Giám tổ chức, Hiệp hội Xúc tiến phát triển Điện ảnh Việt Nam chủ trì nội dung. Tiến sĩ Lê Xuân Kiêu - Giám đốc Trung tâm Hoạt động Văn hóa Khoa học Văn Miếu - Quốc Tử Giám - là trưởng ban tổ chức. Điểm cốt lõi của cuộc thi không nằm ở việc minh họa di sản mà là khả năng khơi gợi một cuộc đối thoại.

title: Madras High Court upholds permission to reconstruct church near Hindu temple
content:
3 min readNew DelhiUpdated: Sep 7, 2026 10:56 AM IST

The constitutional guarantee of peaceful coexistence of persons professing different faiths cannot be curtailed merely based on an unproven apprehension, the Madras High Court has held while dismissing a plea against permission granted for the reconstruction of a Christian prayer hall located about 45 metres away from a Hindu temple.
Justices M Dhandapani and N Dilip Kumar passed the order on a plea filed by a district executive committee member of an organisation named Hindu Munnani, challenging an order of the Sivagangai District Collector granting permission for the reconstruction of a church building in Dhayapuram village.
“The apprehension expressed by the petitioner regarding a possible law and order problem, by itself, cannot be a ground to interfere with an administrative order, particularly when the competent authority has considered the relevant materials and the field inspection report does not disclose any such existing dispute or objection from the local residents,” the order dated August 25 read.
Justices M. Dhandapani and N. Dilip Kumar refused to interfere with order granting permission for church reconstruction.
Why court refused to interfere?
The matter reached the High Court in 2021. In April 2021, the court directed the district administration to lock and seal the premises after the petitioner filed a plea alleging that the reconstruction of the church building was undertaken without obtaining prior permission from the district collector.
The court then allowed the respondent (not named in the ruling) to seek permission from the District Collector to reconstruct the prayer hall. Following the permission, the petitioner sought directions to quash the order, arguing that permitting a Christian prayer hall in such proximity to the temple would cause law-and-order issues in the locality.
The respondents, however, submitted that a prayer hall had existed at the site for around 25 years and that the construction in question was merely a reconstruction of the old building, which had become structurally weak.
The court noted that a field inspection had found that the temple and the prayer hall were about 45 metres apart. It also noted that the local residents had informed the authorities that worship had been conducted at the site for around 25 years and that they had no objection to the continuation of the prayer hall.
