The bench held that there was no evidence to show that the construction or use of the prayer hall violated any statutory provision or that the district collector’s order was contrary to the directions issued by the High Court in the earlier proceedings.
“In the absence of any material to establish that the construction or use of the prayer hall is in violation of any statutory provision or that the impugned order has been passed contrary to the specific directions issued by this Court in the earlier writ petition, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the decision of the District Collector,” it said.
Rejecting the petitioner’s apprehension on the possible law and order problem, the ruling held that it was no ground to interfere with an administrative order, adding that the petitioner was not a resident of the locality and had failed to place material demonstrating any illegality, procedural irregularity, arbitrariness or violation of the court’s earlier directions.

title: One last goodbye to old Hannam before 6,000 homes rise
content:
Demolition 99 percent complete as residents revisit a disappearing hillside community through photographs, food and childhood games
Hannam-dong is now synonymous with some of Seoul’s most expensive homes. But photographs displayed outside its community center reveal a neighborhood filled with hillside shacks, aging houses and longtime residents who are now saying their goodbyes.
Much of the neighborhood preserved in those photographs is now gone. Demolition in Hannam District 3 was 99 percent complete as of mid-September, and the Seoul Metropolitan Government aims to begin construction by the end of December.
Covering about 386,000 square meters across Hannam-dong and neighboring Bogwang-dong, the project will replace the old neighborhood with a residential complex of nearly 6,000 homes.
Around 50 photographs line the walkway leading to the Hannam-dong Community Service Center. They range from images of tightly packed homes climbing the hillside to a photograph of the Seoul Central Mosque upon its completion in 1976, beneath a banner reading “Celebrating the completion.”
Opened on May 21 that year, the Seoul Central Mosque was Korea’s first mosque. It has been excluded from the redevelopment project and is set to remain, even as most of the surrounding low-rise neighborhood is replaced.
“Redevelopment had been talked about for decades, but it kept being delayed. Now that the buildings are gone and the mosque can be seen from almost anywhere, it finally feels real,” said Kim Jung-ho, a Hannam-dong native and longtime resident.
Kim helped run the three-day event, titled “Bye Hannam, Hi Hannam,” which ended Friday. The program brought different generations together through the photo exhibition, nostalgic street food and traditional childhood games.
It offered longtime residents a chance to revisit the neighborhood they remembered, while allowing children and younger visitors to experience an earlier way of life.
Lee Eun-kyung, head of a local women’s association and a graduate of Hannam Elementary School, prepared jeon, or Korean-style savory pancakes, and other foods residents remembered from childhood.
“We stand at the threshold of a new chapter,” Lee said.
“We wanted those who stayed and those who had moved away to come together once more, share a plate of jeon and leave with one last memory of the neighborhood.”
For people who remember Hannam-dong before it became a byword for wealth, the photographs also document the scale of its transformation.
“The neighborhood has already changed enormously since I was a child, and with nearly 6,000 homes coming in, it is set to change even more,” said Kim Kyu-sik, who was born in Hannam-dong and has lived there his entire life.
“There were many shacks and aging houses when I was growing up. Now Hannam-dong is known simply as an affluent area.”
The established luxury enclaves most closely associated with Hannam-dong, including Hannam The Hill, Nine One Hannam and UN Village, lie outside the redevelopment area.
The new project has nevertheless drawn considerable attention in the property market. Some residents and local real estate agents expect larger homes in the complex to eventually be valued at around 7 billion won ($5 million). Of the nearly 6,000 homes planned, about 1,000 will be public rental units.
Hannam District 3 is part of the broader Hannam New Town project, originally divided into five redevelopment zones covering about 1.1 square kilometers across Hannam-dong, Bogwang-dong and nearby neighborhoods.
The area was designated as a new town in 2003, but the project was repeatedly delayed by disputes involving the redevelopment association and builders, as well as lengthy approval procedures.
District 3 is expected to be the first to begin construction, while projects in Districts 2, 4 and 5 are proceeding at different stages.
“The Seoul Metropolitan Government, district offices and redevelopment associations will work as one team to swiftly resolve obstacles on the ground,” said Kim Seong-bo, Seoul’s second vice mayor for administrative affairs. “We will closely manage each project through completion to accelerate housing supply across the city.”
For longtime residents, however, the arrival of thousands of new homes will also mark the end of the community captured in the photographs.
“Once the new complex is built, most of the residents will be newcomers,” Kim Kyu-sik said. “With property values having risen so much, many of the original homeowners sold their properties and left.”

title: Los españoles elegidos para representar a Die Linke en Berlín: “Sí que hay manera de frenar a la ultraderecha”
content: Jaime Martínez y Luis Sanz, españoles residentes en Berlín, han salido elegidos como representantes en dos distritos de Berlín y Pilar Caballero, alemana de ascendencia española, participará en el parlamento de la capital alemanaLa ultraderecha vuelve a ganar en Alemania y la CDU de Merz sufre un descalabro histórico Si por algo es conocido Berlín, además de por la música electrónica, es por su diversidad y multiculturalidad. Y, consciente de ello, Die Linke (La Izquierda) ha querido aprovechar ese filón para conectar con partes de la población que han estado más desconectados de la política local. Las elecciones locales de Berlín han presentado una oportunidad excepcional para Die Linke, que ganó la semana pasada por primera vez en toda la capital alemana y en más de un tercio de los barrios, que cuentan con sus propias competencias como planificación urbanística, servicios sociales y movilidad, entre otros. Con la vivienda y la limpieza de las calles como asuntos centrales, la formación liderada por la turco-alemana Elif Eralp ha conseguido el 25,7% de los votos. Dos emigrantes españoles y una hispano-alemana figuran en las listas de concejales y parlamentaria electos: Jaime Martínez, palentino; Luis Sanz, madrileño; y Pilar Caballero, berlinesa hija de españoles. Jaime Martínez lleva trabajando en la Universidad Libre de Berlín desde 2016, milita en Die Linke desde 2019 y espera participar de la política local de Steglitz. Luis Sanz, que tuvo que emigrar con la crisis económica a Berlín, ciudad que le acogió hace 13 años, será uno de los concejales del barrio de Neukölln, un barrio multicultural del sur de la capital alemana. Ambos militaban en Izquierda Unida antes de afiliarse, en Alemania, a Die Linke. De hecho, Jaime Martínez encabezó la lista provincial de IU en Palencia a las Cortes de Castilla y León en 2019. Pilar Caballero es hija de inmigrantes españoles y, como ella sí es alemana, ha podido presentarse para la cámara de Diputados de Berlín. Los tres destacan el trabajo que ha hecho su partido durante años para llegar hasta este punto y destacan la estrategia específica para estos comicios. “Hemos emulado el ejemplo de Mamdani”, apunta Martínez. Aunque Die Linke tenía más de cien propuestas, se ha centrado dos temas concretos: la vivienda y el servicio de limpieza, que atiende de manera desigual a los barrios pudientes y obreros, una idea englobada en el eslogan de Die Linke, 'Hacer Berlín asequible'. “Tras las elecciones de Sajonia-Anhalt, se lanzó una campaña antifascista, pero no solo se trataba de ir a la contra, sino de 'entendemos que hay un descontento, pero queremos generar un espíritu constructivo'”, explica este palentino. Uno de los grupos de militantes y voluntarios de Die Linke que han trabajado en la estrategia de puerta a puerta. Al fondo, a la izquierda, Jaime Martínez. Los tres españoles reconocen la excepcionalidad berlinesa después del crecimiento de la extrema derecha en Sajonia-Anhalt y en el estado de Mecklemburgo-Antepomerania, donde Alternativa por Alemania (AfD) ha conseguido el 38,2% de los votos. Luis Sanz recuerda que más del 80% de la población de Berlín vive de alquiler, por eso la vivienda es una cuestión tan importante en la zona. “Berlín es una ciudad, y aquí el problema más importante es el de la vivienda. Los alquileres están demasiado altos y hay demasiada poca regulación”, reflexiona Pilar Caballero: “Y la estrategia de ir puerta a puerta y escuchar a la gente aquí ha funcionado. Les hemos preguntado por sus problemas”. Die Linke quiere implementar el referéndum de 2021 y expropiar a los tenedores de más de 3.000 viviendas. Los jóvenes y las mujeres han sido dos de los grupos sociales que más han apoyado a Die Linke en Berlín, que también ha tenido crecimiento de voto entre las personas con formación superior y trabajadores por cuenta ajena. “En Sajonia-Anhalt, AfD ha arrasado entre las personas que tienen condiciones de vida más precarias, y en Berlín hemos ganado nosotros en ese grupo, aunque aún llegamos menos a los pensionistas, y tenemos que ver si tiene más relación con la historia y el Muro”, apunta Martínez. Campaña en 400.000 puertas Aupado por activistas, asociaciones, grupos sociales y organizaciones de inmigrantes como el Bloque Latinoamericano de Berlín, Die Linke ha querido mostrar la diversidad que vive y convive en Berlín y ha visto la necesidad de ser una referencia para sus habitantes: sus oficinas se han convertido en puntos de información sobre cómo afrontar los imposibles del alquiler o cómo pedir ayudas sociales, mientras la estrategia de ir puerta a puerta ha funcionado de manera muy positiva. En dúos, los militantes de Die Linke se han personado en unas 400.000 puertas de Berlín para escuchar las demandas de sus ciudadanos y plantear sus propuestas. Sanz también destaca que Die Linke tiene marcado un sueldo máximo para sus representantes, y la diferencia va a la financiación del partido y a inversiones en los barrios. Entre sus primeras medidas, Eralp plantea reforzar los topes del alquiler, trabajar contra la usura del alquiler, mejorar la limpieza, una 'gira' de escucha por Berlín y mejorar la atención a las personas sin hogar. “Ahora hay que no defraudar, que es complicado por lo difícil de la cuestión. No queremos ser un partido protesta, pero queremos canalizar la protesta”, sostiene Sanz. Jaime Martínez, en una imagen de campaña de Die Linke. Para Martínez, el crecimiento de AfD no es “imparable”, aunque sí reconoce que las políticas de conservadores (CDU) y socialistas (SPD) está generando “un caldo de cultivo de desesperanza, cabreo e indignación”. “Hay gente que no tolera más recortes sociales y que los trenes cada vez sean más impuntuales mientras se invierte en gasto militar. Si a esa frustración le sumas el racismo estructural, los discursos de extrema derecha o la arabofobia calan”, explica Jaime Martínez. Luis Sanz vive en Neukölln, el distrito de Europa con la mayor comunidad palestina, en el que hay más de 300.000 habitantes y que en muchas ocasiones es criminalizado por parte de los partidos de extrema derecha. En ese distrito, ha ganado la candidatura de Die Linke de la mano del palestino Ahmed Abed con un 32% del voto, aunque aún no está claro si podrá ser elegido alcalde de distrito, porque necesita el apoyo del resto de formaciones. En el barrio, el segundo partido ha sido la CDU, con un 15% del respaldo. “Neukölln es un ejemplo de lo que es Berlín”, defiende Sanz. “En el centro de la ciudad el voto suele ser verde o socialdemócrata. Y en la periferia hay mezcla de burguesía venida a menos y una clase trabajadora. Y es la historia de siempre, ¿cómo llegas a todos? No llegábamos a la periferia, pero en algunas zonas hemos pasado de un 3% a un 18%, siendo parte del granero de la extrema derecha, que aumenta bastante, pero se queda lejos respecto a otras regiones. Si uno se consigue plantear como alternativa, sí que hay una manera de frenar a la extrema derecha”. Imagen de Luis Sanz durante un mitin político. Ahora toca pensar en el futuro más próximo: en las negociaciones para acordar qué áreas dirigirá cada partido dentro de los barrios y cómo se configura el nuevo gobierno de Berlín, porque buena parte de los berlineses busca cambios grandes en la ciudad. “Hay que no defraudar la esperanza. La gente tiene que notar que la vida cambia. Si no conseguimos que noten que pueden vivir mejor, de alguna manera, en cinco años la situación será diferente. La responsabilidad es muy grande”, remata Martínez.

title: How MrBeast built $10 million village in Ghana for families affected by child labour
content:
YouTube creator Jimmy Donaldson, better known as MrBeast, unveiled a nearly $10 million village in Ghana as part of an initiative to help families affected by child labour in the cocoa industry.
Called Abna Dakwa Village, the project provides housing, education, healthcare, clean drinking water and livelihood opportunities. MrBeast documented the initiative in a new video and described it as his largest humanitarian project to date.
The village was built on previously undeveloped land following about a year of planning and eight months of construction. It includes 10 free homes for teachers, a medical clinic, a community marketplace and a school equipped to educate more than 300 children.
To encourage children to attend school, students at the village school will receive free daily meals for the next five years. The Rockefeller Foundation has supported the programme.
The development also includes an off-grid solar power system, installed with support from the Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet. Two large water towers have been built to provide clean drinking water, while agricultural facilities and fish tanks are intended to help the community become more self-sufficient.
The project is also linked to MrBeast’s chocolate company, Feastables, which has promoted ethically sourced cocoa and raised concerns over child labour in the cocoa supply chain.
In the video, MrBeast highlighted the broader problem of children working in hazardous conditions on cocoa farms in West Africa and called on consumers and chocolate companies to take greater responsibility.
“Big chocolate will not care about rampant child labour until you guys watching this video do something about it,” he said, urging viewers to demand greater accountability from chocolate manufacturers.
Child labour remains a concern in cocoa-producing regions of West Africa. The International Labour Organisation and UNICEF have documented children’s involvement in hazardous agricultural work in the region.
The YouTuber said Abna Dakwa Village aims not only to provide infrastructure but also to address economic pressures that can push children into agricultural labour instead of education.
The village was developed in partnership with the 1 Billion Followers Summit, the Varkey Foundation and Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives under the 1 Billion Acts of Kindness campaign. Ten other content creators from around the world also travelled to Ghana to help build the village.

title: On Sign Language Day, an interpreter recalls a moment on stage with the President
content:
When President Droupadi Murmu delivered her address at the first convocation of the Central Tribal University of Andhra Pradesh in Visakhapatnam in June, Ms. K.V.L. Suchitra Balakrishna stood beside her on the dais, rendering the Hindi-language speech into sign language as it was spoken. “Within a fraction of a second, I was able to translate it,” she said, recalling the moment the Governor, the State’s Education Minister and the Union Education Minister were also present.
Ms. Suchitra, says she signs fluently in five languages, Telugu, Hindi, English, Odia and Bengali, believes that range was why officials chose her for the assignment.
For Suchitra Balakrishna, founder of the Prajwal Vani Welfare Society and Trust, the assignment capped a lifetime around sign language. Her elder sister, Padmaja, is hearing impaired, and the two attended the same special school in the 1990s. A 1996 assignment to choreograph ‘Hum Honge Kamyaab’, a song in sign language for her deaf classmates, she said, convinced her that schools should not segregate children by disability. “This education gave me my livelihood,” she said. “Today, it placed me beside the President of India.”
That personal history has led into advocacy work now sharpened around this year’s International Day of Sign Languages, observed on September 23 under the theme “Declaring Deaf People’s Human Rights”.
The day also marks the World Federation of the Deaf’s 75th anniversary and 20 years since the UN adopted the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. Against that backdrop, India’s shortage of trained interpreters, Ms. Suchitra said, remains severe: Visakhapatnam has only two or three, Andhra Pradesh fewer than ten, against an all-India count the Indian Sign Language Research and Training Centre has put it at under 300.
Much of her outreach, she said, has gone into corporate awareness sessions, including for Biocon’s two Visakhapatnam units, and sign-language training in government schools across Parawada for students in Classes VIII to X, an effort she said now covers every school there. She also leads an annual session at NTPC’s summer camp for adolescent girls, hoping repeated exposure will normalise the language beyond the deaf community.
The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, recognises sign language as a means of communication for the hearing impaired, and Ms. Suchitra argues its provisions, including interpreter positions in government schools, colleges and departments, remain largely unimplemented nine years on. She has been seeking land in Visakhapatnam to expand the training work, a request she said has gone unanswered for close to two decades.
“Give us respect,” she said, speaking of persons with disabilities more broadly. “Not charity. That is all we are asking, for every child.”

title: ‘At school, I’m a teacher – with Auckland, I’m a teammate’
content:
When Eloise Blackwell debuted for the Auckland Storm rugby team in 2009, current teammate Emacyn Ieremia wasn’t even born.
And Ieremia isn’t just a teammate – she is a student at a school where ‘Mrs Blackwell’ is on the teaching staff.
Blackwell teaches and coaches Ieremia at Epsom Girls’ Grammar School, which won its maiden Auckland First XV championship this year.
On Saturday, Blackwell’s extraordinary longevity will be highlighted when she celebrates her 100th game for Auckland in the fourth round of the Dame Farah Palmer Cup (FPC) against Bay of Plenty at Eden Park.
Blackwell is just the second Auckland woman behind Fiao’o Fa’amausili (ONZM) to reach a century of appearances since the team’s inception in 1987. In 2017, Blackwell and Fa’amausili won a Rugby World Cup together as Black Ferns – the highlight of Blackwell’s 46 test international career that stretched from 2011 to 2021.
“It’s crazy to think I’ve been around as long as some of my teammates have been alive,” Blackwell laughed.
“A hundred games was never something I thought about or talked about, so to suddenly join Fi as the only one to do it is amazing. She’s a great player; she went to five Rugby World Cups.
“The teacher-student dynamic is interesting but balanced with a clear understanding that at school I’m a teacher; with Auckland I’m a teammate. The way I interact as a teammate might differ from how I interact in class, but respect and care still apply.
“Why do I keep going? I still believe I have something to offer. I’m keen to share what I know with those coming through. When I started, I was lucky that the Black Ferns were a regular part of the NPC. I learned from legends like Victoria Heighway and Vita Dryden. If younger players can learn something from me, I’m useful. Of course, knowledge goes both ways. I’m still learning from them.”
Blackwell grew up on Great Barrier Island, where her family lived from 1865. She lived there until she was 13, moving away to study at Mercury Bay Area School in Whitianga because there was no secondary school on the island. She spent years 12 and 13 playing rugby in Canada.
She joined Ponsonby to play rugby and netball in 2008 and debuted for Auckland a year later in a 41-9 win against Manawatū. She laughs: “I got 20 minutes at the end. I didn’t do my job.”
Auckland routinely won the FPC at the start of Blackwell’s career, securing Premierships every year from 2011 to 2015. The arrival of Counties Manukau, North Harbour, Northland, and Bay of Plenty as FPC unions, with fewer Black Ferns involved due to professionalism, has diminished Auckland’s dominance.
Still, Blackwell, who has 71 wins and 23 tries for Auckland, was established as a regular Black Fern by 2011, sharing several Tests with longtime Auckland teammate Charmaine Smith.
Smith recalls: “When I first started playing rugby, I nearly broke my neck after being cleaned out at a ruck. It was my fault. I was in the wrong position because I was still learning. I remember reflecting on what happened and decided to learn the right techniques, especially around contact. Eloise made that easier. She’s precise and detailed in everything she does. She explains difficult things simply and, most importantly, has great patience,” Smith said.
Between 2017 and 2022 Canterbury won the FPC Premiership five times. In 2023, Blackwell and Auckland finally broke an eight-year title drought in Christchurch, with Blackwell scoring two tries in her favourite Auckland game, a 39-27 final win.
“I’ve always had a love-hate relationship with Canterbury. I love playing them; I hate losing to them. They have always been a big rival for Auckland. In ’23 we did something special by going down there and beating their Black Ferns-stacked side.
“When you look at our team – Braxton Sorensen-McGee, Katelyn Vaha’akolo, Patricia Maliepo, Sylvia Brunt, Maia Roos, Ma’ama Vaupulu, Liana Mikaele-Tu’u – these girls have gone on to achieve special things with the Blues and the Black Ferns. That FPC was their breakthrough.
“The FPC without Black Ferns does feel a little bit watered down from what it was, but it remains a pivotal stepping stone and development pathway. I’m really excited by the young talent coming through.”
Blackwell is not only helping nurture that talent at first-class level. In her day job as a physical education teacher at EGGS, she has also taken on the role of First XV coach. This year, as well as winning that Auckland title for the first time, Epsom finished third at the National Top Four, defeating Christchurch Girls’ High School, who had attended every tournament since 2018, in a playoff match.
“We’re not doing anything special like academies or recruiting. We’re just working hard and creating a good experience and culture for the girls. I guess women’s rugby has had a lot of positive publicity lately, which helps attract good players,” Blackwell said.
Epsom is not renowned as a rugby school, but Blackwell has patiently built a program that is growing in numbers and reputation. Emacyn Ieremia and Mikaya Tonga are in the Auckland FPC squad with Blackwell.
Auckland was humbled 36-19 by Canterbury in the opening round of this year’s tournament. Blackwell acknowledged the performance was “below par.” A 37-36 upset of defending champions Waikato was a perfect response. In a game with nine lead changes, a 76th-minute try by prop Glory Aiono earned Auckland maximum competition points. Last Saturday, Counties Manukau was dispatched 46-26, with Blackwell scoring a try.
“We’ve got an exciting game plan and a good mix of youth and experience. We’re learning to better balance the desire for all-out attack with more kicking and orthodox strategy. Our biggest weakness is making too many mistakes by trying to do too much,” she explained.
Few have done more for Ponsonby Rugby Club than Blackwell. She credits Ponsonby with her success. It cultivated her love of the game and taught her the importance of service, tradition, and hard work.
Blackwell has played 117 senior club games, winning four Coleman Shields. The first in 2020 broke a 28-year drought without the title. When the “Fillies” won in 2025, they joined Marist (1999-2001) as the only other club to win a hat-trick of Coleman Shields. Ponsonby scored at least six tries in every match, something none of their other 18 undefeated champion Premier teams, men or women, can claim. The 2025 Fillies also scored at least 30 points every time, another first for the club, and beat their main rivals comprehensively each time, never winning by fewer than 10 points.
Additionally, Blackwell is a recognised leader at all levels of the club. She has served on committees, volunteered countless hours, and organised holiday coaching programmes for girls aged 13-17. These are always fully booked and very successful.
In 2025, she became the 12th person to have the double distinction of Centurion and Life Member on her blazer pocket. The others are Percy Tetzlaff, Sir Bryan Williams, Trevor Paterson, Keith Nelson, Lin Colling, Murray Menzies, Jack Huch, Joe Stanley, Andy Haden, Grant McCurrach and Grant Rutherford. That group includes six All Blacks and one Manu Samoa representative.
Paul Neazor is one of New Zealand’s pre-eminent rugby historians. A proud Ponsonby stalwart, he’s written extensively about a club that has won 12 Auckland senior female championships and produced 24 Black Ferns, not to mention their 48 All Blacks and 52 senior men’s championships.
“I believe Eloise has been a trailblazer for the women’s game in this country, refusing to accept bit roles and second-class status in what was a pretty macho world when she first started making her way in the game,” Neazor said.
“Her efforts have gone a long way to building not just the club’s strengths but also Auckland and the Black Ferns. Blackwell is a real student of lineout play and therefore a dominant figure in this area. She does all that is expected in the tight, and covers the ground surprisingly quickly in broken play. Seldom stood down unless injured, she has been one of the key players in the New Zealand game.”

title: Mike Hammer Engages with Families Receiving Humanitarian Aid in Villa Clara
content:
Mike Hammer, the chief of mission at the U.S. Embassy in Cuba, visited the municipality of Corralillo in Villa Clara this past weekend, particularly the town of Quintín Banderas. His visit aimed to connect with families who benefited from U.S. humanitarian aid packages and ensure the assistance reached those in dire need.
The Embassy captured Hammer's visit in a video shared on its X account, under the hashtag #ConCubanosDeAPie. The footage shows Hammer engaging in conversations with the aid recipients inside their homes.
The visuals highlighted the precarious conditions these families face daily. One woman expressed her gratitude to Hammer upon receiving the aid, saying, "I cried so much. The need is overwhelming," and mentioned that before receiving the package, she had nothing left to eat. Another recipient shared her experience trying the sardines included in the food module.
"Being close to Cubans and listening to them is fundamental to our work," the Embassy noted when posting the video, appreciating the families for "opening their homes and welcoming us warmly."
Follow-Up on Aid Distribution in Villa Clara
This visit was a direct follow-up to the distribution that began in Villa Clara on September 10, when 700 food kits and 700 hygiene kits arrived at Abel Santamaría Airport, targeted for families in Quemado de Güines and Rancho Veloz.
Hammer had previously toured the province from September 12 to 14, visiting vulnerable households in Quemado de Güines and the Cotorra neighborhood. He also met with Bishop Arturo González Amador, the director of Cáritas Santa Clara, and dissident Guillermo "Coco" Fariñas, who had been detained on August 31.
Challenges and Future Aid Plans
During that visit, the Cuban regime launched a disinformation campaign against Hammer in Villa Clara, falsely claiming the food was contaminated—a claim publicly refuted by Cáritas.
The aid Hammer oversees is part of a $100 million program announced by the Trump administration for Cuba. Of this, $60 million is directed through the Catholic Church via Cáritas Cuba and Catholic Relief Services, while $40 million is channeled through other independent organizations, bypassing the Cuban state.
On September 16, the Embassy revealed plans to extend aid to five additional provinces: Camagüey, Ciego de Ávila, Cienfuegos, Matanzas, and Pinar del Río. Shortly thereafter, Cáritas Cienfuegos distributed nearly 700 kits in the Lajas municipality.
Scope and Limitations of the Aid Program
The program is expected to benefit between 100,000 and 120,000 families across Cuba, prioritizing elderly individuals living alone, people with disabilities, pregnant or nursing women, and families with children under five.
Bishop González Amador has cautioned, however, that the assistance has clear limitations: "We can only help the most urgent and distressing cases," stressing that "this is not a permanent social assistance project."
Frequently Asked Questions About U.S. Humanitarian Aid in Cuba
What is the goal of Mike Hammer's visit to Villa Clara?
Mike Hammer's visit aimed to ensure that U.S. humanitarian aid reached those in need and to engage with the families who benefited from the aid packages.
How was the aid distributed across Cuba?
The aid is part of a $100 million program, with $60 million distributed through the Catholic Church and $40 million through other independent organizations, prioritizing vulnerable groups throughout the island.
What challenges have been faced during the aid distribution?
The Cuban regime attempted a disinformation campaign claiming the food was contaminated, which was publicly refuted by Cáritas.

title: DR Congo’s power-hungry mining sector drives record solar surge
content:
DR Congo’s power-hungry mining sector drives record solar surge
More than 300,000 solar panels and 120 battery containers are helping to power Africa’s largest copper mine with continuous clean energy in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as miners turn to solar as an alternative to expensive diesel and energy imports.

The clean electricity is displacing millions of litres of polluting diesel and costs less than a fifth of the price of generator power per kilowatt hour, the mining company said.

More than 300,000 solar panels and 120 battery containers are helping to power Africa’s largest copper mine with continuous clean energy in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as miners turn to solar as an alternative to expensive diesel and energy imports.
The project at the Kamoa Copper mine in the south of the DRC, which became operational last month, is one of the largest solar and battery facilities generating baseload power on the continent.
The clean electricity is displacing millions of litres of polluting diesel and costs less than a fifth of the price of generator power per kilowatt hour, the mining company said.
The project is part of a massive solar deployment across the continent. Recent data from global energy think-tank Ember found record solar capacity of 17 GW will be installed in Africa this year – a 45% rise from 2025.
Installed by CrossBoundary Energy, a developer of distributed renewable energy systems, the solar-battery facility at the DRC mine is “proof of concept” that solar and battery systems can provide the reliable power at scale needed by remote industrial operations, Annebel Oosthuizen, managing director at Kamoa Copper, told Climate Home News in an interview.
“There's always been this perception in the DRC that solar isn't ideal because it is raining half of the year. But it's perfectly ideal. We are seeing a lot of interest from other mines that are still depending on generators and power imports,” she said.
Mining drives solar and battery surge
Like Kamoa Copper, a growing number of miners in the DRC are looking to solar power to compensate for the country’s chronic energy deficit at a lower cost as global diesel prices hit record highs amid ongoing attacks on oil infrastructure in the Middle East.
As a result, the mining sector has become a key driver of the country’s growing clean energy demand and one of the biggest importers of large-scale solar equipment.
Ember found the DRC is set to install a record 1.7 gigawatts (GW) of solar panels this year – a 544% increase compared to 2025 and the equivalent of adding more than 60% of the country’s entire 2023 grid capacity.
The deployment of combined solar and battery storage solutions to deliver stable energy supplies to mines has also caused battery imports to surge. In dollar terms, the DRC’s imports of batteries from China far exceeded that of solar in the year to June 2026, according to Ember.
A crippling power deficit
The DRC holds significant energy resources and some of the world’s largest reserves of the minerals required to manufacture clean energy technologies. It is the world’s largest producer of cobalt, which is needed to make batteries, and Africa’s top producer of copper – a metal sought after for its electrical conductivity which is pivotal to the world’s electrification efforts.
Yet just 22.5% of the DRC’s population had access to electricity in 2024 – one of the lowest rates in the world, according to the World Bank. And as mining expands and more of the minerals extracted are being processed in the country, unreliable power supply has become a major constraint for the sector, which contributed to more than a quarter of the country’s GDP in 2024, excluding oil and gas.
The country has enormous hydropower potential, with the hydroelectric potential of the Congo River estimated at around 100 GW. But only a fraction is being harnessed.

Still, virtually all of the DRC’s grid-connected electricity is generated by hydropower by the state-owned utility, Société Nationale d'Électricité (SNEL).
The electricity then has to be transported more than 1,500 kilometres to reach the mining belt in the south – a challenge made more difficult by ageing grid infrastructure and limited transmission capability. SNEL did not respond to a request for comment.
“It is estimated that there’s around a 1 GW energy deficit for the DRC mining sector,” said Matt Tilleard, CEO of CrossBoundary Energy, which owns the solar and battery equipment at the Kamoa Copper mine and provides the power as a service.
“The interest in solar from the mining industry is not theoretical – it is already translating into large-scale solar and battery procurement for mining operations in the region,” he added.
Solar displaces gas, saves energy costs
The facility installed by CrossBoundary is part of a plan by Kamoa Copper to supply more of the electricity it needs with solar energy and batteries as its operations expand, a faster solution than relying on harder-to-build hydropower projects.
"Our processing capacity has increased drastically over the last couple of years. We've constructed the largest copper smelter in Africa and that is so power-intensive,” said managing director Oosthuizen.
A joint venture between Canadian firm Ivanhoe Mines, Chinese company Zijin Mining Group and the DRC government, the mine needs 235 megawatts (MW) of power, which is expected to nearly double to 450 MW in the next five years.
Kamoa Copper currently receives 100 MW from state utility SNEL - “and the rest we have to find a solution for”, said Oosthuizen.
Another 30 MW solar and battery baseload facility is expected to come into operation this month, enabling around 25% of the mine's power needs to be generated by solar energy. An additional 60 MW of continuous solar power will be added by the end of 2027, and the company is exploring options for more solar capacity and two hydropower projects.
The operational 30 MW of clean electricity provided by CrossBoundary Energy will power pumps that prevent 400 million litres of water from flooding the underground mine every day.
In August alone, the facility has reduced the mine’s diesel consumption by around four million litres, generating an estimated $11 million dollars in savings at current diesel prices, Oosthuizen said.
The mine still relies on generators to meet a 20-40 MW deficit and to power the trucks used in the mine, which Oosthuizen said would be difficult to electrify in the next five years because the technology isn't yet ready to operate in the mine's tough and wet conditions.
Avoiding a two-speed transition
To prevent a major imbalance between industrial players’ access to clean, reliable energy and the millions of Congolese who remain without power, the government requires private electricity producers to reserve at least 10% of their generated power for local communities living near rural production sites.
Delivering this, combined with rural electrification, mini-grid development and national grid expansion, is critical to prevent a two-speed energy transition that leaves people behind, said Catherine Mukobo, head of ACERD, the Congolese Association for Renewable and Decentralised Energies.
“Without implementing these policies, the DRC could get in a situation where mines have access to abundant modern energy while a large part of the population remains without electricity,” she said.

title: Nach Brand: Neues Clubheim eröffnet
content:
Der Brand zwang den Verein zu provisorischen Lösungen für den Sportbetrieb. Die Stadt und der Verein begannen schnell mit den Planungen für den Wiederaufbau. Das neue Gebäude wurde in Holzbauweise auf der bestehenden Struktur errichtet, und wo möglich, wurden bestehende Bauteile weiterverwendet.
Moderne Infrastruktur
Laut Aussendung der Stadt bietet das neue Clubheim mit etwa 960 Quadratmetern Platz für Umkleiden, Vereinsräume, Gastronomie sowie Lager- und Technikräume. Ein begrüntes Flachdach, eine Photovoltaikanlage und Luft-Wasser-Wärmepumpen sind Teil des nachhaltigen Konzepts. Somit verfügt die Admira wieder über die nötige Infrastruktur für Trainings- und Spielbetrieb sowie für das Vereinsleben.
SC Admira Dornbirn feiert neues Sportheim
Bedeutung der Gemeinschaft
Bei der Eröffnung stand die Gemeinschaft im Vordergrund. Viele bekannte Gesichter kamen zusammen, Erinnerungen wurden geteilt und natürlich wurde über Fußball gesprochen. „Nach dem Brand war für uns klar, dass wir die Admira beim Wiederaufbau rasch unterstützen wollen. Umso schöner ist es, jetzt zu sehen, wie das neue Clubheim wieder mit Leben gefüllt wird“, sagte Bürgermeister Markus Fäßler (SPÖ).
Neue Perspektiven
Sportstadträtin Barbara Röser (ÖVP) betonte die Bedeutung der Admira: „Die Admira steht seit 80 Jahren für Fußball, Nachwuchsarbeit und ein starkes Miteinander.“ Auch Hochbaustadtrat Christoph Waibel freute sich über den Abschluss des Projekts: „Nachhaltigkeit wurde dabei von Beginn an mitgedacht – von der Holzbauweise über die Photovoltaikanlage bis zur Wärmeversorgung."

title: Atgimė 650 metų istoriją menantis Sendvario dvaras
content:
Rugsėjo 17-ąją Klaipėdoje oficialiai atidarytas atkurtas Sendvario dvaras – viena seniausių miesto dvarviečių, kurios istorija siekia 1376 metus. Į penkerius metus trukusį dvaro atkūrimą investuota 20 mln. eurų. Šiandien 10 000 kv. m teritorijoje veikia apie 70 verslų, o dvaras miestui sugrįžta kaip gyva, atvira erdvė, jungianti istorinį paveldą, šiuolaikinę architektūrą, verslą ir miesto gyvenimą, rašoma Sendvario dvaro pranešime žiniasklaidai.
Sendvario dvaro istorija prasidėjo prieš 650 metų. Per šimtmečius čia keitėsi šeimininkai, santvarkos, pastatų paskirtys ir pats Klaipėdos miestas. Dvaras išgyveno klestėjimo laikotarpius, karus, gaisrus ir ilgus tylos metus.
2021 metais prasidėjęs dvaro atkūrimas tapo naujausiu šios istorijos etapu. Jo tikslas nuo pat pradžių buvo ne sukurti uždarą istorinį objektą, o išsaugant vietos tapatybę sugrąžinti ją į kasdienį miesto gyvenimą.
Sendvario dvaro sugrįžimą į miesto gyvenimą atidarymo ceremonijoje sveikino ir Klaipėdos miesto meras Arvydas Vaitkus.
„Aš neabejoju, kad šį gražų ansamblį, šias erdves ir pastatus pamils ne tik klaipėdiečiai, bet ir miesto svečiai. Tikiu, kad čia gims naujos idėjos ir mintys, kaip toliau puošti ir kurti mūsų nuostabų Lietuvos uostamiestį“, – sakė A. Vaitkus.
20 mln. eurų investicija į istorinės vietos atgimimą
Per penkerius metus į Sendvario dvaro atkūrimą „Augama“ investavo 20 mln. eurų.
Projekto metu rekonstruoti du istoriniai pastatai – dvaro rūmai ir ūkinis pastatas. Neišlikusių istorinių pastatų vietose iškilo nauji statiniai, o bendras sukurtų erdvių plotas siekia apie 10 000 kv. metrų.
Šiandien Sendvario dvaro užimtumas siekia apie 90 proc. Teritorijoje jau veikia apie 70 skirtingų verslų – restoranai, parduotuvės, sveikatos, grožio ir sveikatingumo paslaugų teikėjai, kūrėjai bei įvairių sričių įmonių biurai.
Atkurti ne vien pastatus, bet ir vietos charakterį
Projektuojant teritoriją siekta išsaugoti tai, kas Sendvaryje buvo vertingiausia – istorinius pastatus, dvaro struktūrą, senus medžius ir teritorijos charakterį – kartu suteikiant jai šiandien reikalingas funkcijas.
Teritorijoje išsaugoti brandūs medžiai, atkurtos alėjos, buvusio dvaro prūdelio vietoje įrengtas fontanas, sukurtos pėsčiųjų, poilsio ir viešosios erdvės.
Architektūrinę Sendvario atkūrimo viziją kūrė „UP architektai“ ir „Uostamiesčio projektas“, interjerais rūpinosi „Dopro architektai“.
Ryšys tarp seno ir naujo išlaikytas ne tik pastatų architektūroje. Dalis autentiškų medžiagų, kurių nebebuvo įmanoma panaudoti pagal pirminę paskirtį, įgavo naują gyvenimą interjere. Iš senųjų pastatų sijų likučių pagaminti vienetiniai baldai ir kiti interjero elementai. Rūmuose atkurta istorinė priemenė, o rūsyje numatyta įrengti konferencijų salę.
Nauju Sendvario simboliu tapo „Sparnuotas žirgas“
Vienu pagrindinių oficialaus atidarymo akcentų tapo specialiai Sendvario dvarui sukurto „Sparnuoto žirgo“ atidengimas.
Skambant muzikai į dvaro kiemą įjojo raiteliai ant žirgų, o tarp jų buvo atidengtas skulptoriaus Martyno Gaubo sukurtas sparnuotas žirgas.
Žirgo motyvas pasirinktas neatsitiktinai – jis tiesiogiai susijęs su istorine dvaro praeitimi ir čia puoselėtomis žirgininkystės tradicijomis.
Skulptorius M. Gaubas pasakojo, kad žirgo idėja projekte atsirado dar pačioje pradžioje. Sparnai kūrinyje simbolizuoja sėkmę ir polėkį, tačiau skulptoriui buvo svarbios ir tvirtos žirgo kojos – priminimas, kad norint kažką sukurti ir pasiekti neužtenka vien talento, reikia daug dirbti.
M. Gaubo kūriniai eksponuojami galerijose ir viešosiose erdvėse, jo darbų yra ir Valdovų rūmų muziejaus fasade.
Atidarymo ceremonijos metu Sendvario dvaras buvo pašventintas, o į stiebą pakelta Sendvario dvaro vėliava.
Atidarymo dieną dvaras atsivėrė miestui
Oficialaus atidarymo diena prasidėjo atvirų durų programa klaipėdiečiams. Miestiečiai galėjo vaikščioti po atkurtą teritoriją, susipažinti su dvaro istorija, aplankyti čia įsikūrusius verslus ir dalyvauti jų organizuotose veiklose.
Vėliau vyko oficiali Sendvario dvaro atidarymo ceremonija, subūrusi dvaro atkūrimo komandą, architektus, partnerius, verslo bendruomenę ir kviestinius svečius.
Vakarinėje atidarymo programoje pagrindinis dėmesys buvo skirtas 650 metų Sendvario dvaro istorijai. Per muziką, vaizdus ir pasakojimą svečiams buvo pristatyti skirtingi dvaro gyvavimo etapai – nuo jo ištakų iki šiandieninio atgimimo. Vakaro programą papildė atlikėjos Monikos Liu pasirodymas.
Nuo galvijų kiemo iki bajoriškojo dvaro
Sendvario ištakos siekia 1376 metus, kai Klaipėdos pilies inventoriuje buvo paminėtas Viehof – galvijų kiemas. Ši ūkinė teritorija buvo glaudžiai susijusi su Klaipėdos pilimi ir miesto gyvenimu.
Vėliau čia formavosi administraciniai ir gyvenamieji pastatai, o 1723 metais buvo įkurtas Sendvario valsčius, apėmęs 125 kaimus.
1807 metais, Klaipėdoje apsistojus Prūsijos karališkajai šeimai, Sendvaryje buvo įrengtas princams skirtas jodinėjimo maniežas. 1817 metais Sendvariui suteiktas bajoriškojo dvaro rangas.
Žirgai ilgainiui tapo neatsiejama Sendvario istorijos dalimi – dvare buvo auginami veisliniai žirgai, vykdavo žirgų turgūs.
Pirmasis pasaulinis karas dvarui buvo negailestingas – 1915 metais sudegė dvaro rūmai ir dalis ūkinių pastatų. Vėliau išlikę pastatai keitė paskirtis ir buvo naudojami įvairioms reikmėms, tačiau vientisas dvaro gyvenimas ilgainiui užgeso.
Nepraleiskite svarbiausių kultūros naujienų ir gaukite jas kiekvieną penktadienį į savo elektroninio pašto dėžutę užsisakę LRT kultūros naujienlaiškį. Šio naujienlaiškio nenorėsite atsisakyti.

title: Mirziyoyev Reviews Mahalla Development in Nukus District
content:
Tashkent, Uzbekistan (UzDaily.uz) — President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the Diyqan Arna mahalla in Nukus district on 18 September during a trip to the Republic of Karakalpakstan, where he reviewed efforts to develop infrastructure, create jobs and increase household incomes, the press service of the President of Uzbekistan said.
More than 1,000 families, comprising over 3,600 people, live in the mahalla. Projects being implemented there are aimed at improving living conditions, creating employment opportunities and raising residents’ incomes.
The mahalla has introduced the Smart Mahalla system, which uses digital technologies to process citizens’ appeals promptly, maintain demographic records and monitor infrastructure. The system is also used to support the development of entrepreneurship.
Modernization of social infrastructure is continuing. Under the investment programme, a modern kindergarten with 60 places was built at a cost of 4.5 billion soums. Another 1 billion soums from the local budget was allocated for the construction of football and workout facilities.
Beekeeping has become one of the main sources of income growth under the “One Mahalla — One Product” principle. More than 20 households currently raise bees. Each keeps between 50 and 100 hives, producing up to 1 tonne of honey annually.
The President visited the home of mahalla resident Bakhtiyar Zhubaev, where he reviewed a honey-processing workshop and the production of beehive boxes.
During one season, the workshop sells 2 tonnes of processed honey, generating around 200 million soums in annual profit. It also produces more than 250 beehive boxes each year, bringing in up to 80 million soums in additional revenue.
By the end of the year, the Beekeepers Association plans to organize beekeeping in another 100 households on a cooperative basis. This is expected to provide an additional number of families with a stable source of income.
During the visit, Mirziyoyev also met with mahalla activists, representatives of the older generation and young people.
The discussions focused on the further development of the area and improving the well-being of the population.
It was noted that the development of the Aral Sea region and improving the living standards of its population remain among the priorities of state policy.
According to the President, development work in mahallas will expand, while the pace of implementation will accelerate.

title: I missed spending time with my adult son, so I hired him as my golf instructor
content:
When my now 23-year-old son returned from college, I noticed he was more independent. While this is what every parent wants, it also means fewer interactions between us.
He now got up on his own without me knocking on his door, made his own egg sandwiches in the morning, and drove himself everywhere. I was no longer the alarm clock, the cook, or the chauffeur.
He was planning to move out of our house soon to get his first apartment in Los Angeles and leave behind boring suburbia. I knew he needed extra cash because he was still looking for a job, and I was desperate to spend some quality time with him. Then I had an idea.
"I need you to teach me golf," I said one morning.
"Are you serious?" he asked.
"Yes, and I'll pay you," I offered.
Golf lessons were easy money for my son
My son has been golfing since he was 4. For me, it was a practical choice. I wanted him to play a sport where he had less of a chance of getting hurt, and golf was one that he could potentially play well into adulthood. He took to it and ended up eventually playing on his high school team.
When I pitched the idea of paid lessons, he jumped at the chance, motivated by the need to fill his gas tank. Plus, my new golf clubs had been sitting in my garage for two years, a gift from my husband one Christmas when we discussed what we would do when we retire.
Being a master negotiator like his dad and a skilled salesman like his stepdad, he locked in a higher rate than I initially offered. If I were taking lessons from a golf pro, it would cost twice as much, which is not in my budget right now. I was not about to squabble over a few bucks, since I figured he'd get that money out of me another way anyway.
Golf gave us a new way to connect
We worked together to determine a date and time that worked for both of us. I get up at 5 am. He wakes up at noon. I work 9 to 5. He wasn't working — yet. The weekends were best, and I talked him into a 9 a.m. start time, before the Southern California sun tried to burn our scalps off.
At 10:30 a.m. on our agreed-upon day, he sleepily carried my clubs and loaded them into my SUV, and we were on our way.
During the first lesson, he explained what each club did. Then we covered my grip and stance and moved on to the complicated swing.
"You have to keep your arm straight and loosen your hands," he said more than once.
I also had to, "Choke up, keep my eye on the ball, bend my knees, graze the grass, and not hit it so hard! It should feel effortless!" he said.
I was used to a bat as a softball player. Smashing a ball was all I knew. With all the tips and corrections he gave, I started to love every minute of our lesson. Not because I was learning golf, but because I was learning more about my son. He was patient and so knowledgeable. He also noticed every tiny thing I did wrong and explained it to me clearly until he couldn't, like when I asked him to show me what I did wrong after the ball went in a completely different direction than intended.
"Mom, I can't even describe how bad that shot was. Let's just move on and try it again."
That made us both laugh.
The lesson became something more
After the lesson, he carried my clubs to the car as if he were my caddy.
"That was really fun," he said. "Should we go to brunch?" he asked, surprising me.
I already had a bagel for breakfast that morning, but I jumped at the chance to spend more time with him. Over eggs Benedict, we talked about the résumés he had sent out, when his girlfriend was moving to California, and when our next lesson would be.
For our first lesson, we spent three hours together. I can't remember the last time that happened. I took out my phone, transferred the money to his account, and felt like our day was a hole-in-one.
We had weekly lessons until he moved out of our house a few months later. We plan to start up again once the weather cools down where we live. Of course, I'll have to pay extra for gas now that he has to drive to me. But I don't mind, the time we get to spend together is priceless.

title: Angola: Over 2.5 Million Angolans Update Voter Registration Data
content:
Malanje — At least 2.5 million Angolan citizens aged 18 and over across the country have already updated their data as part of the Official Voter Registration process, which has been under way since June.
The information was provided in Malanje by the National Director of Official Voter Registration, Pascoal Santana, at the end of a visit by Minister of Territorial Administration Daniel Félix Neto to assess the progress of the process in the province.
According to the director, technical and material conditions are currently being put in place to enable Communal One-Stop Public Service Centres (BUAP) to become operational in the coming days.
He said that, alongside the fixed service, mobile data registration teams have been prioritising recondite areas.

title: Αποτέφρωση: Από ταμπού, κανονικότητα
content:
Συνεχής αύξηση του αριθμού των ανθρώπων που επιλέγουν τη μετά θάνατον καύση παρατηρείται στη χώρα μας τα τελευταία χρόνια, ακολουθώντας – έστω και με σχετικά αργά βήματα – την τάση στην υπόλοιπη Ευρώπη. Αυτό αποτυπώνεται και από το γεγονός ότι μετά το αποτεφρωτήριο της Ριτσώνας, που επί χρόνια υπήρξε μονοπώλιο, από τον περασμένο Νοέμβριο λειτουργεί και δεύτερο, στην Αλεξάνδρεια Ημαθίας, καλύπτοντας τις ανάγκες της Βόρειας Ελλάδας.
Σημειώνεται πως μέχρι το 2019, όταν άρχισε να λειτουργεί η μονάδα στη Ριτσώνα, όσοι επιθυμούσαν να αποτεφρωθούν αναγκάζονταν να πηγαίνουν σε γειτονικές χώρες, κυρίως στη Βουλγαρία. Η κατάσταση, όμως, φαίνεται πως αλλάζει, μαζί με τις συνήθειες. «Από εκεί που ήταν ταμπού, πλέον εμπεριέχει στοιχεία κανονικότητας», λέει στα «ΝΕΑ Σαββατοκύριακο» ο Αντώνης Αλακιώτης, πρόεδρος της Ελληνικής Κοινωνίας Αποτέφρωσης και του αποτεφρωτηρίου της Ριτσώνας.
Ο ίδιος παρέθεσε μάλιστα και κάποιους αριθμούς που καταδεικνύουν την αύξηση. Έτσι, ενώ το 2020 μόλις το 2,2% των θανόντων πανελλαδικά αποτεφρώθηκε, το 2025 το αντίστοιχο ποσοστό ήταν 5,71% και φέτος αναμένεται να ξεπεράσει το 6,3%. Το παραπάνω επιβεβαιώνεται και από τα δημόσια οικονομικά στοιχεία. Με βάση αυτά, το 2025 η εταιρεία Crem Services SA, που διαχειρίζεται το αποτεφρωτήριο της Ριτσώνας, είχε κύκλο εργασιών σχεδόν 5 εκατομμυρίων ευρώ, μια αύξηση της τάξης του 9,76% σε σχέση με το 2024 – ενώ αύξηση υπήρξε επίσης και στα κέρδη της εταιρείας, που το 2025 έφτασαν τα 2,1 εκατ. (μετά τους φόρους), έναντι 1,95 εκατ. το προηγούμενο έτος.
Γιατί, όμως, ολοένα περισσότεροι επιλέγουν την καύση; Οσοι μας μίλησαν, συνηγορούν ότι ο βασικός λόγος δεν είναι άλλος από την ανάγκη των οικογενειών να αποφύγουν τη διαδικασία εκταφής. Κάτι που ενδεχομένως νιώθουν ως «εκκρεμότητα», ενώ παράλληλα έχει τόσο οικονομικό όσο και ψυχολογικό κόστος. «Η αποτέφρωση δεν έχει ιδεολογικό ή θρησκευτικό περιεχόμενο», ξεκαθαρίζει ο Αλακιώτης.
«Πολλές οικογένειες, ειδικά νεότεροι άνθρωποι, δεν θα μπουν στη διαδικασία ταφής και εκταφής, δεν θέλουν να ζήσουν για δεύτερη φορά την απώλεια του ανθρώπου τους. Και βέβαια με την αποτέφρωση, μπορούν να σκορπίσουν ένα κομμάτι από τις στάχτες στη θάλασσα ή σε άλλο μέρος που ήθελε ο εκλιπών ή και να τις φυλάξουν στο σπίτι», προσθέτει από μεριάς του ο Νίκος Αγγελέτος, πρόεδρος της Ενωσης Λειτουργών Γραφείων Κηδειών Ελλάδος. Βέβαια υπάρχουν και πιο… ιδιαίτερες περιπτώσεις, όπου η τέφρα ζητείται να μεταποιηθεί σε κοσμήματα ή μέχρι και σε διαμάντια.
Χαμηλό ποσοστό και αντιδράσεις
Σε κάθε περίπτωση, παρ’ όλο που η Ελλάδα ακολουθεί τους ρυθμούς άλλων χωρών της Δυτικής Ευρώπης, τα ποσοστά αποτέφρωσης στη χώρα μας παραμένουν ακόμη χαμηλά και βέβαια η παραδοσιακή ταφή συνεχίζει να είναι κυρίαρχη. Στην κορυφή της σχετικής λίστας, σύμφωνα με στοιχεία της Κοινωνίας της Αποτέφρωσης για το 2024, βρίσκονται χώρες της κεντρικής και βόρειας Ευρώπης, όπως η Σλοβενία (87,19% των νεκρών) και η Δανία (87, 94%), ενώ τα ποσοστά μειώνονται σταδιακά προς Νότο και Ανατολάς – Ισπανία (50,11%), Ιταλία (38,94%) και Βουλγαρία (6,63%).
Οπως εξηγεί ο πρόεδρος του ΔΣ του αποτεφρωτηρίου της Ριτσώνας, το 75% της πελατείας του είναι από την Αθήνα και τον Πειραιά. Τον Νοέμβριο του 2025, το «μονοπώλιο» της Ριτσώνας έσπασε το αποτεφρωτήριο στην Αλεξάνδρεια Ημαθίας. Το «κενό» στη Βόρεια Ελλάδα εντόπισε ο Σπύρος Ζερβός, ο οποίος άνοιξε τη συγκεκριμένη επιχείρηση, την οποία λέει πως είδε ως «πολιτιστική επένδυση». Στο σύντομο διάστημα που λειτουργεί, παρατηρεί ότι υπάρχει αύξηση του ενδιαφέροντος για την αποτέφρωση, ωστόσο δεν είναι κάτι το οποίο μπορεί ακόμα να αποτυπώσει στατιστικά.
«Υπήρξαν κάποιες, όχι έντονες, αντιδράσεις, οι οποίες πυροδοτήθηκαν από την εκκλησία, αλλά η τοπική κοινωνία σύντομα κατάλαβε ότι εδώ γίνεται μια διαδικασία με σεβασμό και αξιοπρέπεια και χωρίς να υπάρχει κάποια επιβάρυνση του περιβάλλοντος», αναφέρει στα «ΝΕΑ Σαββατοκύριακο».
Τα σχέδια που κατέρρευσαν
Σημειώνεται ότι παλιότερα υπήρχαν σκέψεις να ανοίξουν και δημοτικά αποτεφρωτήρια – μεταξύ άλλων στην Αθήνα, στου Ζωγράφου, στη Θεσσαλονίκη, στην Πάτρα και την Κρήτη – ωστόσο τα σχέδια κατέρρευσαν ή έχουν μείνει στα χαρτιά για πολεοδομικούς, πολιτικούς ή και οικονομικούς λόγους.
«Πέρα από τις αντιδράσεις που υπάρχουν, είναι και δύσκολο να βρεθεί ο κατάλληλος χώρος, ο οποίος θα είναι μακριά από κατοικίες. Επίσης, προς το παρόν, οι ανάγκες στη χώρα μας καλύπτονται από τα ήδη υπάρχοντα αποτεφρωτήρια», προσθέτει. Στο παραπάνω συμφωνεί και ο Ζερβός: «Στην επαρχία δεν είναι τόσο συνηθισμένο, οπότε δεν συμφέρει τόσο ως επένδυση και επιπλέον υπάρχει δυσκολία στις σχετικές αδειοδοτήσεις».
«Σίγουρα πρέπει να ανοίξει κάτι πιο κοντά στην Αθήνα, γιατί πολλές οικογένειες ταλαιπωρούνται για να έρθουν μέχρι τη Ριτσώνα», σημειώνει από την πλευρά του ο Αλακιώτης. Μάλιστα, το 2024, η Crem Services SA επιχείρησε να προχωρήσει στη δημιουργία ιδιωτικού αποτεφρωτηρίου και στον Ασπρόπυργο, το σχέδιο όμως βρίσκεται «στον πάγο», καθώς εκκρεμούν δικαστικές αποφάσεις, λόγω αντιδράσεων περιβαλλοντικών οργανώσεων, κατοίκων και της τοπικής αυτοδιοίκησης. «Παρ’ όλες τις δυσκολίες, όταν γίνει κανονικότητα και το επιλέγει περισσότερος κόσμος θα ανοίξουν και άλλα αποτεφρωτήρια. Είναι ανάγκη των καιρών», προσθέτει.

title: Men incarcerated in Kansas heard families owed $6,000 for lunch, raised funds to help
content:
A group of men incarcerated in Kansas saw a problem in their community and stepped in with money from their own pockets to help solve it.
After learning that Norton Community Schools had accumulated roughly $6,000 in unpaid meal costs, they organized a fundraiser that erased most of the debt.
Here's what to know
On Aug. 3, nearly 30 men incarcerated at Norton Correctional Facility gathered to present Superintendent Corey Roy with a check for $4,267 to put toward the district's unpaid meal accounts.
As local news outlet KWCH reported, an effort to raise the funds was organized through Reaching Out from Within, an organization that has been operating in prisons across Kansas, North Carolina, and Missouri for over four decades to enable member-led healing and rehabilitation.
In the recent Norton fundraiser, individuals participating in the program donated $3,810, and staff from the Kansas Department of Corrections contributed another $457, according to KWCH. With that gift, the district was able to clear the majority of its meal debt, which built up as the school provided breakfasts and lunches to students experiencing food insecurity at home.
More background
A statement shared by the correctional facility noted that many of the men who had donated said they had gone hungry when they were young and believed it had hurt their performance in school. They hoped their efforts would help to ensure that food insecurity would not be a barrier for students as they began the new academic year.
"I was moved at how the men I spoke with wanted to make a positive impact to help others in the community," Roy also said in the statement.
As economic pressures, compounded by energy shocks and hits to agricultural production, contribute to rising food costs across the country, more families are experiencing the strain at home.
At the same time, more than 1.5 million children — and around 5 million people overall — are estimated to have lost access to support through the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, since the One Big Beautiful Bill Act became law in 2025. The estimates were published by the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities last month.
Families could feel even more pressure related to the loss of federal benefits by the end of September, when many SNAP program costs are set to shift to states.
No nationwide solution for school meal debt has yet passed Congress. Many districts still rely on local responses such as donations, nonprofit partnerships, and direct aid for families.

title: ICIJ journalist Micah Reddy freed after 4 days in secretive Djibouti custody
content:
ICIJ Africa coordinator and journalist Micah Reddy has been released from custody in Djibouti.
Reddy, who had been held secretly after being detained on Saturday, flew out of the country today following his release.
Reddy arrived in Djibouti on Sept. 17 and went silent around 1 p.m. local time on Sept. 19, along with his local assistant, Mohamed Willo Ismael (“Kooki Mahmoud”).
Ismael is understood to be free as well.
ICIJ raised the alarm within hours of the two men’s disappearance from the Escale International Hotel in Djibouti City, when messages to the pair went unanswered.
On Sept. 21, ICIJ confirmed unofficially through diplomatic and other channels that Reddy was in custody, understood to be held for failing to obtain proper media accreditation.
The South African, British and U.S. governments all assisted in reaching out to Djiboutian authorities for information.
Djibouti authorities did not publicly confirm his whereabouts or provide access to Reddy until today.
The many calls for press freedom and for the men’s swift release are an example of the solidarity that matters when a journalist’s safety is put at risk.
—ICIJ director Gerard Ryle
Reddy’s family expressed its relief at his and Ismael’s release but dismay over his treatment and the secrecy surrounding it.
They thanked helpers on the ground, the South African and UK governments, press freedom organizations, ICIJ and the many journalists who had assisted.
They also thanked Reddy’s legal team for its international efforts.
“Waiting for news of a loved one whose whereabouts and wellbeing are unknown is unimaginably painful,” the Reddy family statement said.
“We are profoundly grateful that, for our family, this story has had a happy ending.”
ICIJ echoed the Reddy family in expressing its gratitude to all whose vocal response helped both to discover that Reddy had been held secretly in custody and to secure his freedom.
“The many calls for press freedom and for the men’s swift release are an example of the solidarity that matters when a journalist’s safety is put at risk,” ICIJ director Gerard Ryle said.
Ryle thanked the staff of the U.S. Embassy in Djibouti for their assistance in securing the release of Reddy.
He added his thanks to South African diplomat Zane Dangor, to the U.K. Embassy in Washington DC and to its consular services in London.
Ryle added that four days in secretive custody is unacceptable treatment for any investigative journalist.
And he thanked Reddy’s wife Nicole and brother Niall for their immense efforts to secure Reddy’s release, and their stoic forbearance under extreme pressure.
The Committee to Protect Journalists, Human Rights Defenders, Reporters Without Borders, Gift of the Givers and Amnesty International were among the organizations that assisted in these efforts.
Many reporters also lent their aid, notably South African publisher and journalist Branko Brkic.
At this stage, all the details and circumstances of Reddy’s arrest are unknown. But he and his local guide are safe, healthy and free.

title: Lahore enjoying dengue ebb
content: The metropolis has recorded a sharp decline in dengue cases and deaths in recent years, according to data compiled by the Metropolitan Corporation of Lahore. The data shows that Lahore had witnessed a major outbreak in 2021, when 20,042 dengue cases and 118 deaths were reported. Most cases were recorded in the areas of Cantonment, DHA, open spaces and rural localities. The number of cases fell to 8,252 in 2022, while deaths dropped to 24. In 2023, 7,031 cases and six deaths were reported. The situation improved further in 2024, with only 475 cases recorded and no deaths. Last year, 781 dengue cases and three deaths were recorded. Available data for the ongoing year shows 23 cases so far, with no death reported. Officials attributed the decline to coordinated action against mosquito breeding sites. Lahore DC Mohammed Ali Ejaz said all necessary measures, including efforts to prevent larval breeding, were continuing. He stressed the importance of public cooperation, saying timely identification and cleaning of potential breeding sites could help reduce the risk of a resurgence. Awareness campaigns were being conducted to encourage citizens to take preventive measures, he added. A former deputy commissioner, Syed Musa Raza, said the administration had focused on practical measures. He said surveillance and cleanliness at cemeteries, lakes, ponds, residential and commercial areas and other potential mosquito-breeding sites had been strengthened. According to Raza, authorities had also directed the hospitals to report dengue patients and laboratory results. Whenever dengue larvae or a patient was identified, preventive measures were initiated in the affected area, including spraying around the infected household and neighbouring homes. He said more than 200 open ponds and stagnant-water sites across the city had been cleared, while the cleaning of drains was also carried out in coordination with the Water and Sanitation Agency. Former Mayo Hospital medical superintendent Dr Ehteshamul Haq said dengue could only be effectively controlled by ensuring that both larvae and patients were identified and reported rather than concealed.

title: Free rail travel extended to bereaved military families this Remembrance weekend
content:
Free rail travel extended to bereaved military families this Remembrance weekend
Bereaved military family members will be able to travel by train free of charge this Remembrance weekend, helping them attend services and commemorative events to honour loved ones who died while serving in the Armed Forces.
Hundreds of bereaved military family members will be able to travel by train free of charge this Remembrance weekend (7-8 November), helping them attend memorial services and commemorative events to honour loved ones who died while serving in the Armed Forces.
For the first time, one next of kin of a service person who died while serving will be able to travel free of charge on National Rail services to attend Remembrance weekend events.
The move builds on the existing free travel offer for serving personnel and veterans, giving people breathing space and ensuring travel costs are not a barrier for families taking part in remembrance and reflection.
Minister for Veterans and People, Calvin Bailey, said:
“Remembrance is an opportunity for the nation to come together in recognition of the service and sacrifice of our Armed Forces. For bereaved families, this is a deeply personal time.
“We must never forget that behind every name we remember is a family whose lives have been changed forever. Providing free rail travel will help bereaved relatives come together and honour their loved one without financial barriers.”
Mikki Brett, the widow of the late CPO Stuart Brett, who served in the Weapons Engineering branch of the Royal Navy and died in service in April 2023, spoke with Minister Bailey this week. She said:
“It’s fantastic news that the in-service bereaved have been recognised for the support given to their loved ones with free train fares to remembrance events this year.”
Mikki is already registered to come to the Cenotaph on Remembrance Sunday, and will benefit directly from the new travel offer for those bereaved in service.
A spokesperson for SSAFA, the Armed Forces charity said:

title: Por unanimidade, STF iguala tempo de licenças-maternidade e adotante
content:
Publicidade
O Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) decidiu nesta quarta-feira (23) unificar os prazos de licença-maternidade e licença-adotante para mulheres.
Por unanimidade, os ministros julgaram procedente uma ação da Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) para igualar o tempo dos benefícios.
Pelo entendimento firmado pela Corte, mães genitoras e adotantes têm direito às licenças remuneradas de 120 dias, que podem ser prorrogadas por mais 60 dias, independentemente do tipo de vínculo trabalhista.
O prazo deve ser contado a partir do parto ou obtenção da guarda. Nos casos de internação da mãe, o prazo vale a partir da alta da mãe ou do bebê, o que ocorrer por último.
Conforme a decisão, a nova regra vale para licenças futuras e para as que estão em andamento.
Entenda
A ação julgada pela Corte foi protocolada pela PGR em outubro de 2023 e pretendeu estender o tempo das licenças-maternidade e adotante previsto na Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT), regra da iniciativa privada, para as outras categorias, como as servidoras públicas, que são regidas pela Lei 8.112/1990.
Continua depois da publicidade
Pela CLT, as mães biológicas e adotantes têm direito a 120 dias de licença, prazo que pode ser prorrogado por mais 60 dias em empresas que participaram do Programa Empresa Cidadã. Já as servidoras gestantes também podem tirar 120 dias, mas as adotantes só têm direito a 90. No caso do Ministério Público, a licença adotante cai para 30 dias.
Para PGR, o tratamento desigual em relação ao regime de contratação da mulher é inconstitucional.
Julgamento
O julgamento da ação começou na última quarta-feira (16), quando o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, relator do caso, proferiu o seu voto.
Continua depois da publicidade
No entendimento do ministro, as licenças têm objetivo de criar vínculo afetivos entre mães e filhos e não podem possuir prazos diferenciados.
Em seguida, os ministros Flávio Dino, Dias Toffoli e Cármen Lúcia acompanharam o relator.
Na sessão de hoje, os ministros Cristiano Zanin, André Mendonça, Nunes Marques, Luiz Fux e Gilmar Mendes proferiram seus votos, e o julgamento foi encerrado.

title: Bačić o zaštićenim najmoprimcima: Stan u Zagrebu može se otkupiti za 74.000 eura
content:
Bačić o zaštićenim najmoprimcima: Stan u Zagrebu može se otkupiti za 74.000 eura
POTPREDSJEDNIK Vlade i ministar Branko Bačić obišao je danas nekoliko lokacija namijenjenih stambenom zbrinjavanju zaštićenih najmoprimaca. Rekao je da država treba osigurati 1300 nekretnina, a dosad je riješen 391 zahtjev. Plan je, kaže, sve zahtjeve riješiti do kraja desetljeća.
Prema zakonu kojim se rješava pitanje zaštićenih najmoprimaca, nakon presuda Europskog suda za ljudska prava i Ustavnog suda, oni mogu birati između nekoliko rješenja: isplate umjesto stana, useljenja u državni stan ili dogovora s vlasnikom o nastavku najma ili otkupu stana.
Bačić je rekao da se najveći broj zaštićenih najmoprimaca odlučio za jednokratnu isplatu. "Ovisno o broju članova kućanstva imali su značajne popuste i ljudi su preuzeli, odnosno imali su pravo i ministarstvo ih je isplatilo u potpunosti", rekao je Bačić.
Useljenje u državne stanove
Dio najmoprimaca odlučio se za useljenje u državne stanove. Do konačnog rješenja plaćat će najamninu od dva eura po četvornom metru, a imaju i mogućnost otkupa stana po povoljnijim uvjetima. Bačić je kao primjer naveo stan od 67 četvornih metara u Zagrebu. "Otprilike je cijena tog stana, po tim povoljnim uvjetima, 74.000 eura, što je, složit ćete se, u današnje vrijeme i s obzirom na cijene u Zagrebu, više nego povoljno", istaknuo je ministar.
Dodao je da je plan do kraja desetljeća riješiti svih 1300 zahtjeva. "U ovom trenutku državne nekretnine uređuju 355 stanova. Završili su ih 121, od toga 56 u Zagrebu, i tim ćemo intenzitetom nastaviti kako bi što je moguće više naših sugrađana koji su zaštićeni najmoprimci uselilo u takve stanove", poručio je Bačić.
Najviše zahtjeva, dodao je Bačić, ima u Zagrebu, Splitu i Dubrovniku.
Grade se stanovi u Zagrebu i Splitu
Na lokaciji Blato u Zagrebu trenutačno se gradi višestambena zgrada sa 152 stana. Ravnatelj APN-a Dragan Hristov rekao je da je useljenje planirano za godinu dana. "Riječ je o zahtjevnom objektu neto površine oko 9000 kvadrata. Imat će pet etaža: prizemlje, kat i tri kata. Vrijednost ovog projekta je oko 20 milijuna eura, uključujući i infrastrukturu i priključke koje treba izvesti, a za to se obvezao Grad Zagreb", istaknuo je Hristov.
Dodao je da se nada da će Grad Zagreb na vrijeme odraditi svoj dio posla. U Splitu se također gradi zgrada sa 60-ak stanova, a trebala bi biti završena i useljena najkasnije početkom iduće godine. Na pitanje koliko će cijeli proces zbrinjavanja zaštićenih najmoprimaca stajati, Bačić je odgovorio da to ovisi o lokaciji i troškovima gradnje.
"S druge strane variraju danas i cijene izgradnje, tako da u ovom trenutku ne mogu dati točan podatak, ali evo, ova 152 stana su 20 milijuna eura. Ne možemo to pomnožiti s osam pa da dođemo na tisuću tristo. To bi bilo negdje oko dvjesto milijuna eura, ali ja mislim da neće biti ni puno manje na kraju od toga svega", rekao je Bačić. Dodao je da se cijeli proces financira iz državnog proračuna.
121 državni stan je već završen
Do kraja godine planira se ponuditi i djelomično useliti još oko 107 stanova. Bačić je rekao da je 121 državni stan već završen, dok se još 240 obnavlja ili je u fazi projektiranja.
"Bili bismo najsretniji kada bismo svih ovih 1300 zaštićenih najmoprimaca mogli smjestiti u državne stanove koje obnavljamo. Ali, nažalost, toliko stanova nemamo. Radi se o tome da imamo dosta državnih stanova tamo gdje nema zaštićenih najmoprimaca, odnosno nisu u istoj jedinici lokalne samouprave, a zakon je definirao da zaštićenim najmoprimcima moramo ponuditi nekretninu na području jedinice lokalne samouprave u kojoj žive", pojasnio je ministar.

title: SLC pays £0.8 bn in Maintenance Loan payments to students today
content:
SLC pays £0.8 bn in Maintenance Loan payments to students today
The Student Loans Company (SLC) has paid £0.8 bn in first term Maintenance Loan payments into students’ bank accounts across the UK today (Monday 21 September).
At SLC, the core purpose is to enable opportunity through the delivery of student finance, and today £0.8 billion in Maintenance Loans is being paid to students starting or returning to university.
This is the biggest payment date at the start of the 2026/27 academic year and follows £0.8 billion paid earlier in the month. SLC expects to pay a total of £3bn in maintenance funding by the end of September. Similarly timed payments of £0.9 billion were made in September 2024 and £1.1 billion in September 2025.
Tuition Fee Loan payments are paid directly to higher education providers later in the autumn.
Payments are released to students when their university or college confirms that they have registered/enrolled. Once SLC has this information, it will send a text message to students a few days before the expected payment date to let them know that their Maintenance Loan is on the way. SLC is encouraging students to log-in to their online account to track their application and payment progress. Student can also find more tips on preparing for payment here: Preparing for Payment - GOV.UK
As payments continue, SLC is reminding students to be vigilant of scams targeting their payments. More information can be found at: Students urged to ‘stop and think before you click’ as student finance payments begin - GOV.UK

title: This is how we do it: ‘As a Catholic monk, I was celibate. But sex with Orla feels so natural’

On our first date, last October, I asked Rory how conservative he was and he said: “I have premarital sex, but I’d rather die than eat meat on a Friday.” I’d been single for almost three years and wondered if I’d ever meet someone who understood both sides of me: Catholic but liberal. Sex is one of the ways I make her feel safe and reassure her that she’s beautiful – simply telling her rarely works.

구글 검색에서 연합뉴스 기사를 우선적으로 보여줍니다.
(전남광주=연합뉴스) 정회성 기자 = 24시간 멈추지 않고 가동되는 공장의 생산직 노동자들이 대체공휴일 가산임금을 달라며 회사를 상대로 낸 소송에서 승소했다.
20일 법조계에 따르면 광주지법 민사11부(홍기찬 부장판사)는 A씨 등 1천888명이 금호타이어를 상대로 제기한 임금 청구 소송에서 지난 17일 원고 일부 승소로 판결했다.
A씨 등 원고들은 금호타이어 생산직 노동자이거나 유가족들로, 2022년 1월부터 올해 5월까지 지급되지 않은 대체공휴일 가산임금을 정산해달라며 소송을 냈다.
2014년 첫 시행한 대체공휴일은 2020년부터 민간 기업 노동자에게도 사업장 규모에 따라 단계적으로 유급휴일이 적용됐다.
재판에서 금호타이어 사측은 단체협약 등으로 약속한 휴일을 부여했기 때문에 대체공휴일 근무에 따른 보상을 이행한 것이라고 반박했다.
또 생산직 직원은 일반직에 비해 더 많은 휴일을 보장받고 있어서 적법한 휴식이 이뤄졌다고 강조했다.
이에 A씨 등은 사측이 부여했다고 주장한 휴일은 주야 교대에 따라 보장받은 휴무이기 때문에 대체공휴일 근무와 무관하다고 주장했다.
재판부는 "피고가 직원들에게 대체휴일을 제공했다고 주장하지만, 구체적인 날짜나 이를 정하는 방법 등 어떠한 사항도 단체협약 등에 명시돼 있지 않다"며 노동자들의 손을 들어줬다.
이어 "4조 3교대 형식의 교대 근무는 인간 생체리듬을 역행하는 형태"라며 "일반직보다 많은 휴일을 부여받는 것은 신체 회복 시간의 필요성에 따른 당연한 결과로 보인다"고 판시했다.
금호타이어 노동조합 관계자는 "이번 판결은 병원과 공장처럼 교대제로 24시간 운영되는 사업장의 대체공휴일 가산임금 지급 의무를 명시화한 최초의 사례"라며 "사회 전반으로 확대되는 계기가 되기를 바란다"고 말했다.
노동자들은 이번 소송에서 사측의 상여금 산정 방식도 문제 삼았지만, 이는 재판부로부터 기각됐다.
